items.text:
Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn. This is the mating season of some of the most common varieties, when male house spiders come out of hidden corners to look for females, and garden spiders reach adult size and spin their most dazzling webs.
Yet while the spider is a familiar fixture of nursery poems or songs and Halloween decorations, its relationship with humans is complicated. Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers. Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk. Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless. Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops. But they are a constant source of human anxieties — with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.
Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis? British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them. But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out. And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders.
The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.
Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland. Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas. With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors.
It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds, or butterflies, in spite of their unique status as nature's spinners. But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.

q5.stem: What do we learn about spiders in the UK since the middle ages?
options: They have been generally misconceived.
They have adversely impacted crop growth.
They have been a constant reminder of bad luck.
They have made their presence felt when spinning webs.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk. Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless.」
排除：B 农田蜘蛛捕食竞争作物的害虫，有利而非有害；C 引发焦虑不等于持续预示厄运，非普遍误解锚；D 出现织网属季节现象，与中世纪以来被误解无关。
q5.stemCn: 从中世纪以来，我们从英国的蜘蛛身上了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它们一直被普遍误解。
它们对作物生长产生了不利影响。
它们一直是不祥之兆。
在结网时，它们让人们感受到了它们的存在。

q5.stem: What have spiders been associated with in the UK for centuries?
options: Harm.
Evil.
Suffering.
Aggression.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「But they are a constant source of human anxieties — with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.」
排除：A：与原文相反，蜘蛛几乎无害。；C：张冠李戴，苦难指人类，非蜘蛛关联。；D：无中生有，攻击性未提及。
q5.stemCn: 几个世纪以来，在英国，蜘蛛一直与什么联系在一起？
optionsCn: 伤害。
邪恶。
苦难。
攻击性。

q5.stem: What partly accounts for the reduction in spiders' food supply?
options: The long tradition of collecting insects.
Fast reproduction of their competitors.
Chemicals used for killing insects.
The extinction of a lot of wildlife.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development.」
排除：A：蝴蝶采集传统属他因，非昆虫减少原因；B：天敌快速繁殖原文未提，属无中生有；D：野生灭绝非原文，原文是栖息地破坏
q5.stemCn: 什么部分解释了蜘蛛食物供应的减少？
optionsCn: 收集昆虫的悠久传统。
它们竞争者的快速繁殖。
用于杀虫的化学物质。
大量野生动物的灭绝。

q5.stem: What does the passage say is conservationists' biggest worry?
options: A variety of spiders are threatened due to pollution of marshes and wasteland.
Certain species of spiders are endangered due to loss of their natural homes.
An increasing number of spiders are being killed by deadly pesticides.
More and more spider species are found losing their ability to migrate.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.」
排除：A：污染沼泽荒地无依据，无中生有；C：农药影响昆虫，非直接杀蜘蛛，偷换对象；D：无法迁移是后果，非越来越多。
q5.stemCn: 文章指出，保护主义者最大的担忧是什么？
optionsCn: 由于沼泽和荒地的污染，多种蜘蛛正受到威胁。
由于自然栖息地的丧失，某些蜘蛛物种濒临灭绝。
越来越多的蜘蛛被致命的农药杀死。
越来越多的蜘蛛物种被发现正在失去迁徙的能力。

q5.stem: What wish does the author express close to the end of the passage?
options: More people would recognise spiders' unique status in the ecosystem.
People would show greater enthusiasm for spiders than for butterflies.
There would be sufficient corridors for spiders to move along.
There would be more people appreciating spiders' splendour.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.」
排除：A：偷换概念，未提生态独特地位；B：与原文相反，难及蝴蝶热情；C：细节张冠李戴，非最终愿望
q5.stemCn: 作者在文章结尾处表达了什么愿望？
optionsCn: 更多的人会认识到蜘蛛在生态系统中的独特地位。
人们对蜘蛛的热情会比对蝴蝶更大。
会有足够的通道供蜘蛛移动。
会有更多的人欣赏蜘蛛的壮丽。

items.cn:
蜘蛛在八月底到整个初秋时节都能感受到它们的存在。这是某些最常见蜘蛛品种的交配季节，此时雄性家蜘蛛会从隐蔽的角落出来寻找雌性，而园蜘蛛则长成成年体型，编织出它们最令人惊叹的网。
然而，尽管蜘蛛是儿歌、歌曲和万圣节装饰中常见的元素，它与人类的关系却很复杂。对蜘蛛的恐惧很普遍，并对患者的生活产生严重影响。这种恐惧的普遍性似乎与任何理性的风险评估都无关。英国的蜘蛛几乎都是无害的。农田蜘蛛品种通过捕食与我们争夺作物的昆虫，提供了宝贵的生态系统服务。但它们是人类焦虑的持续来源——与女巫和邪恶的文化联系可以追溯到中世纪。
这是否在一定程度上解释了在我们这个生态危机时代，关于蜘蛛状况的数据缺乏的原因？由于长期以来有收集和观察蝴蝶的传统，英国蝴蝶是世界上研究最多的昆虫群体。但蜘蛛保护主义者指出，直到20世纪80年代，家蜘蛛的分类才得到妥善整理。虽然关于昆虫种群的信息是通过测量撞击挡风玻璃或捕捉装置数量的实验收集的，但很少有人尝试统计蜘蛛的数量。
飞行昆虫数量的巨大减少只能意味着蜘蛛食物供应的减少。最近的一项标志性研究确定了1989年至2016年间昆虫种群下降了75%，农药使用被认为是罪魁祸首之一，同时为开发而破坏野生区域也是原因。这意味着蜘蛛的整体状况令人担忧，就像大多数生物一样。但保护主义者最担心的是那些因栖息地丧失和碎片化而受到威胁的品种，这使得它们无法迁徙。
在英国定期记录的约650种蜘蛛中，大多数在沼泽和荒地中茁壮成长。保护工作通常由坚定的个人领导，通过将它们重新引入新区域，帮助一些物种恢复。随着重新野化现在牢固地列入环境政策议程，希望未来蜘蛛能够自行迁徙，沿着野生动物走廊移动以适应气候变化。
尽管蜘蛛作为自然的编织者有着独特的地位，但它们似乎永远无法像蜜蜂、鸟类或蝴蝶那样吸引同等程度的人类热情。但当它们在这个秋天以全部的辉煌展现自己时，如果更多的动物爱好者认识到蜘蛛的非凡之处，那将是一件好事。

items.title: 2024年6月 六级真题第1套 · 第1篇
items.text:
It is irrefutable that employees know the difference between right and wrong. So why don't more employees intervene when they see someone exhibiting at-risk behavior in the workplace?
There are a number of factors that influence whether people intervene. First, they need to be able to see a risky situation beginning to unfold. Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up. And third, they need to have the communication skills to say something effectively.
This is not strictly a workplace problem; it's a growing problem off the job too. Every day people witness things on the street and choose to stand idly by. This is known as the bystander effect—the more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone in that group is to help the victim. The psychology behind this is called diffusion of responsibility. Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.
This crowd mentality is strong enough for people to evade their known responsibilities. But it's not only frontline workers who don't make safety interventions in the workplace. There are also instances where supervisors do not intervene either.
When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.
Despite the fact that workers are encouraged to intervene when they observe unsafe operations, this happens less than half of the time. Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene. Unsuccessful attempts in the past are another strong contributing factor to why people don't intervene—they tend to prefer to defer that action to someone else for all future situations.
On many worksites, competent workers must be appointed. Part of their job is to intervene when workers perform a task without the proper equipment or if the conditions are unsafe. Competent workers are also required to stop work from continuing when there's a danger.
Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.
Beyond competent workers and supervisors, it's important to educate everyone within the organization that they are obliged to intervene if they witness a possible unsafe act, whether you're a designated competent person, a supervisor or a frontline worker.

q5.stem: What is one of the factors contributing to failure of intervention in face of risky behavior in the workplace?
options: Slack supervision style.
Unfavorable workplace culture.
Unforeseeable risk.
Blocked communication.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Second, the company's culture needs to make them feel safe to speak up.」
排除：A：原文未将松弛监督列为干预因素；C：原文强调能否察觉风险，非不可预见；D：原文指沟通技能不足，非渠道被阻断。
q5.stemCn: 在工作场所面对危险行为时，导致干预失败的因素之一是什么？
optionsCn: 松散的监督风格。
不利的职场文化。
不可预见的风险。
沟通受阻。

q5.stem: What does the author mean by "diffusion of responsibility" (Para. 3)?
options: The more people are around, the more they need to worry about their personal safety.
The more people who witness an event, the less likely anyone will venture to
The more people idling around on the street, the more likely they need taking care of.
The more people are around, the less chance someone will step forward to intervene.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Basically, the larger the crowd, the more people assume that someone else will take care of it—meaning no one effectively intervenes or acts in a moment of need.」
排除：A：原文未提担心安全，只说无人干预。；B：原文指无人帮助受害者，非只是不敢冒险。；C：街头只是举例，非闲人越多越需照顾。
q5.stemCn: 作者在第3段中所说的“责任分散”是什么意思？
optionsCn: 周围的人越多，他们越需要担心自己的人身安全。
目击事件的人越多，有人敢于行动的可能性就越小。
街上闲逛的人越多，他们需要被照顾的可能性就越大。
周围的人越多，有人挺身而出进行干预的机会就越少。

q5.stem: What happens when unsafe behavior at the workplace is not addressed by the leaders?
options: No one will intervene when they see similar behaviors.
Everyone will see it as the easiest way to deal with crisis.
Workers have to take extra caution executing their duties.
Workers are left to take care of the emergency themselves.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「When a group of employees sees unsafe behavior not being addressed at a leadership level it creates the precedent that this is how these situations should be addressed, thus defining the safety culture for everyone.」
排除：B：未处理不强化安全文化，反而形成不干预先例；C：文章仅说担心增加工作，未说主管必须接手；D：胜任人员任命与领导不处理风险无直接因果。
q5.stemCn: 当领导者不处理工作场所的不安全行为时会发生什么？
optionsCn: 当他们看到类似行为时，没有人会进行干预。
每个人都会将其视为应对危机的最简单方式。
工人在执行职责时必须格外小心。
工人只能自行处理紧急情况。

q5.stem: What is the ultimate reason workers won't act when they see unsafe operations?
options: Preference of deferring the action to others.
Anticipation of leadership intervention.
Fear of being isolated by coworkers.
Fear of having to do more work.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Fear is the ultimate factor in not intervening. There is a fear of penalty, a fear that they'll have to do more work if they intervene.」
排除：A：转给他人是失败后的偏好，非最终原因；B：领导未干预只形成先例，不是工人最终原因；C：原文提惩罚和额外工作，未提被同事孤立。
q5.stemCn: 工人看到不安全操作而不采取行动的根本原因是什么？
optionsCn: 倾向于将行动推迟给他人。
期待领导层介入。
害怕被同事孤立。
害怕不得不做更多的工作。

q5.stem: What is critical to ensuring workplace safety?
options: Workers be trained to operate their equipment properly.
Workers exhibiting at-risk behavior be strictly disciplined.
Supervisors create a safety environment for timely intervention.
Supervisors conduct effective communication with frontline workers.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Supervisors also play a critical role. Even if a competent person isn't required, supervisors need a broad set of skills to not only identify and alleviate workplace hazards but also build a safety climate within their team that supports intervening and open communication among them.」
排除：A：偏离原文，未强调设备，而是监督营造安全氛围。；B：原文是营造安全气候，并非惩罚或增加工作。；D：沟通只是氛围的一部分，并非题干关键。
q5.stemCn: 确保工作场所安全的关键是什么？
optionsCn: 培训工人正确操作设备。
严格纪律约束表现出高风险行为的工人。
主管创造一个有利于及时干预的安全环境。
主管与一线工人进行有效沟通。

items.cn:
不可否认，员工知道是非对错。那么，为什么当看到有人在工作场所表现出危险行为时，没有更多员工进行干预呢？
有很多因素影响人们是否进行干预。首先，他们需要能够察觉到危险情况开始发生。其次，公司文化必须让他们感到发言是安全的。第三，他们需要具备有效沟通的技巧。
这不仅仅是工作场所的问题；在职场之外，这也成为一个日益严重的问题。每天，人们在街头目睹各种事情，却选择袖手旁观。这就是所谓的“旁观者效应”——目击某一事件的人越多，该群体中任何人帮助受害者的可能性就越小。这种现象背后的心理学原理被称为“责任分散”。基本上，人群越大，越多人假设别人会处理此事——这意味着在需要时刻无人真正介入或采取行动。
这种群体心态强大到足以让人们逃避其已知责任。但不仅是一线员工不在工作场所进行安全干预，也有主管不进行干预的情况。
当一群员工看到不安全的行为未在领导层得到解决时，这就开创了一个先例，即这类情况应如此处理，从而为所有人定义了安全文化。
尽管鼓励工人在观察到不安全操作时进行干预，但这发生的频率不到一半。恐惧是不干预的最终因素。存在对惩罚的恐惧，以及担心如果干预就得做更多工作的恐惧。过去尝试的不成功是导致人们不干预的另一个强有力的促成因素——他们倾向于在未来的所有情况下将行动推迟给其他人。
在许多工地，必须任命胜任人员（competent workers）。他们职责的一部分是在工人未配备适当设备或在条件不安全的情况下执行任务时进行干预。当存在危险时，也要求胜任人员停止工作继续。
主管也发挥着关键作用。即使不需要指定胜任人员，主管也需要具备广泛的技能，不仅要识别和减轻工作场所的危险，还要在团队内建立一种支持干预和开放沟通的安全氛围。
除了胜任人员和主管之外，重要的是教育组织内的每个人：如果他们目睹可能的不安全行为，他们有义务进行干预，无论是指定的胜任人员、主管还是一线员工。

items.src: 2024年6月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2024年6月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.text:
The term "environmentalist" can mean different things. It used to refer to people trying to protect wildlife and natural ecosystems. In the 21st century, the term has evolved to capture the need to combat human-made climate change.
The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.
On one side are purists who believe nuclear power isn't worth the risk and the exclusive solution to the climate crisis is renewable energy. The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.
Leon Clarke, who helped author reports for the UN's Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, isn't an uncritical supporter of nuclear energy, but says it's a valuable option to have if we're serious about reaching carbon neutrality.
"Core to all of this is the degree to which you think we can actually meet climate goals with 100% renewables," he said. "If you don't believe we can do it, and you care about the climate, you are forced to think about something like nuclear."
The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years. But these cities often have small populations, occasionally still rely on fossil fuel energy and have significant renewable resources at their immediate disposal. Meanwhile, countries that manage to run off renewables typically do so thanks to extraordinary hydroelectric capabilities.
Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy. Chancellor Angela Merkel in 2011 announced Energiewende, an energy transition that would phase out nuclear and coal while phasing in renewables. Wind and solar power generation has increased over 400% since 2010, and renewables provided 46% of the country's electricity in 2019.
But progress has halted in recent years. The instability of renewables doesn't just mean energy is often not produced at night, but also that solar and wind can overwhelm the grid during the day, forcing utilities to pay customers to use their electricity. Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas. The political limit has also been reached in some places, with citizens meeting the construction of new wind turbines with loud protests.
The result is that Germany's greenhouse gas emissions have fallen by around 11.5% since 2010—slower than the EU average of 13.5%.

q5.stem: What accounts for the divide within the scientific community about nuclear energy?
options: Attention to combating human-made climate change.
Emphasis on protecting wildlife and natural ecosystems.
Evolution of the term "green energy" over the last century.
Adherence to different interpretations of environmentalism.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「The distinction between these two strands of environmentalism is the cause of a split within the scientific community about nuclear energy.」
排除：A：关注气候变化只是环境主义演变的一方面，并非分裂根源；B：保护野生动物和生态系统是旧定义，非分裂原因；C：绿色能源演变文中未提，分裂根源是环境主义分歧
q5.stemCn: 科学界对核能产生分歧的原因是什么？
optionsCn: 关注应对人为引起的气候变化。
强调保护野生动物和自然生态系统。
“绿色能源”这一术语在过去一个世纪的演变。
坚持对环境主义的不同解读。

q5.stem: What is the solution to energy shortage proposed by purists' opponents?
options: Relying on renewables firmly and exclusively.
Using fossil fuel and green energy alternately.
Opting for nuclear energy when necessary.
Limiting people's non-basic consumption.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The opposing side agrees that renewables are crucial, but says society needs an amount of power available to meet consumers' basic demands when the sun isn't shining and the wind isn't blowing. Nuclear energy, being far cleaner than oil, gas and coal, is a natural option, especially where hydroelectric capacity is limited.」
排除：A：属纯主义者主张。；B：原文无交替使用。；D：原文未提限制消费。
q5.stemCn: 纯粹主义者的反对者提出的解决能源短缺的方案是什么？
optionsCn: 坚定且排他性地依赖可再生能源。
交替使用化石燃料和绿色能源。
在必要时选择核能。
限制人们的非基本消费。

q5.stem: What point does the author want to make with cities like Burlington as an example?
options: It is controversial whether the goal of the whole world's exclusive dependence on renewables is attainable.
It is contentious whether cities with large populations have renewable resources at their immediate disposal.
It is arguable whether cities that manage to run off renewables have sustainable hydroelectric capabilities.
It is debatable whether traditional fossil fuel energy can be done away with entirely throughout the world.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「The achievability of universal 100% renewability is similarly contentious. Cities such as Burlington, Vermont, have been "100% renewable" for years.」
排除：B：原文未讨论大城市是否拥有充足可再生能源；C：例子没有说明城市是否依赖可持续水电；D：未论证世界是否应彻底禁用化石燃料
q5.stemCn: 作者以伯灵顿等城市为例想要表达什么观点？
optionsCn: 全世界完全依赖可再生能源的目标是否可实现是有争议的。
人口众多的城市是否有可直接利用的可再生资源是有争议的。
能够依靠可再生能源运行的城市是否拥有可持续的水电能力是有争议的。
传统化石燃料能源能否在全球范围内被彻底淘汰是有争议的。

q5.stem: What do we learn about Germany regarding renewable energy?
options: It has increased its wind and solar power generation four times over the last two decades.
It represents a good example of a major industrialized country promoting green energy.
It relies on renewable energy to generate more than half of its electricity.
It has succeeded in reaching the goal of energy transition set by Merkel.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Germany stands as the best case study for a large, industrialized country pushing into green energy.」
排除：A：原文说自2010年风光发电增逾400%，非近二十年翻四倍；C：2019年可再生能源仅占46%，未超过半数；D：转型进展停滞，减排慢于欧盟均值，未达成目标
q5.stemCn: 关于德国的可再生能源，我们了解到什么？
optionsCn: 在过去二十年里，其风能和太阳能发电量增加了四倍。
它代表了主要工业化国家推广绿色能源的一个良好典范。
它依靠可再生能源生产超过一半的电力。
它成功实现了默克尔设定的能源转型目标。

q5.stem: What may be one of the reasons for Germany's progress having halted in recent years?
options: Its grid infrastructure's capacity has fallen behind its development of green energy.
Its overabundance of green energy has forced power plants to suspend operation during daytime.
Its industrial south is used to running factories on conventional energy supplies.
Its renewable energy supplies are unstable both at night and during the day.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Lagging grid infrastructure struggles to transport this overabundance of green energy from Germany's north to its industrial south, meaning many factories still run on coal and gas.」
排除：B：白天电网过剩致倒贴用户，并非电厂暂停运营；C：南部仍用煤气因输电不足，非企业固有习惯；D：夜间不发电、白天过剩，不等于昼夜都缺供应。
q5.stemCn: 近年来德国进展停滞的原因可能是什么？
optionsCn: 其电网基础设施的能力落后于其绿色能源的发展。
其过量的绿色能源迫使发电厂在白天暂停运营。
其工业化的南部习惯于使用常规能源供应运行工厂。
其可再生能源供应在夜间和白天都不稳定。

items.cn:
“环保主义者”这个词可能意味着不同的东西。它过去指的是试图保护野生动物和自然生态系统的人。在21世纪，这个词已经演变，以捕捉对抗人为气候变化的需求。
这两种环保主义流派之间的区别是科学界内部关于核能分歧的原因。
一方面是一些纯粹主义者，他们认为核电不值得冒险，气候危机的唯一解决方案是可再生能源。另一方面同意可再生能源至关重要，但表示社会需要一定量的电力来满足消费者的基本需求，特别是在阳光不照射和风不吹的时候。核能比石油、天然气和煤炭清洁得多，因此是一个自然的选择，尤其是在水电容量有限的地方。
曾参与撰写联合国政府间气候变化专门委员会报告的莱昂·克拉克并非不加批判地支持核能，但他表示，如果我们认真对待实现碳中和，这是一个有价值的选项。
他说：“这一切的核心在于你认为我们实际上能否仅靠100%可再生能源来实现气候目标。”“如果你不相信能做到这一点，并且你关心气候，你就被迫考虑像核能这样的方案。”
普遍实现100%可再生能源供应的可能性同样存在争议。佛蒙特州伯灵顿等城市多年来一直“100%可再生”。但这些城市通常人口较少，偶尔仍依赖化石燃料能源，并且拥有大量即时可用的可再生资源。与此同时，那些成功依靠可再生能源运行的国家，通常得益于非凡的水电能力。
德国作为一个大型工业化国家推进绿色能源的案例研究最具代表性。德国总理安格拉·默克尔于2011年宣布启动“能源转型”（Energiewende），旨在逐步淘汰核能和煤炭，同时逐步引入可再生能源。自2010年以来，风能和太阳能发电量增加了400%以上，2019年可再生能源提供了该国46%的电力。
但近年来进展已停滞。可再生能源的不稳定性不仅意味着夜间往往不产生能源，还意味着白天太阳能和风能可能会使电网过载，迫使公用事业公司向用户付费以使用他们的电力。滞后的电网基础设施难以将这种过剩的绿色能源从德国北部输送到工业化的南部，这意味着许多工厂仍然依靠煤炭和天然气运行。在一些地方，政治限制也已达到极限，公民对新风力涡轮机的建设报以强烈的抗议。
结果是，自2010年以来，德国的温室气体排放量下降了约11.5%——低于欧盟平均水平的13.5%。

items.title: 2024年6月 六级真题第2套 · 第1篇
items.text:
The "American Dream" promises that in the Land of Opportunity, any individual can climb the economic ladder and prosper through hard work and ambition alone. And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.
So why does the idea of the American Dream persist? A new study in the American Journal of Political Science identifies one factor that has been overlooked: the influence of reality TV.
Reality shows have come to dominate US television over the past 20 years, notes Eunji Kim from Vanderbilt University. And the overwhelming majority of these have a "rags-to-riches" storyline: they feature ordinary Americans who work hard to achieve great economic success. And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.
Rags-to-riches stories are ubiquitous(无处不在的) on TV—but does watching these programmes actually convince people that economic mobility is easily attainable? To find out, Kim's team had participants watch a 5-minute clip from a reality show with a rags-to-riches storyline. Control participants watched a clip from a reality show that didn't have a rags-to-riches story. After watching the shows, participants rated how much they agreed with four statements relating to the American Dream.
The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.
Kim also conducted a survey of 3,000 US residents. They also rated the extent to which they believed success in life is related to various internal factors (such as ambition) and external factors (such as family wealth). Finally, they read a list of TV programmes and indicated which they regularly watched.
Participants who were heavy viewers of rags-to-riches programmes or frequent viewers had a stronger belief in the American Dream than those who never watched such shows.
Kim concludes that "rags-to-riches entertainment media are an important cultural force that promotes and perpetuates beliefs in upward mobility". And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.
"In this era of choice, entertainment media is what captures hearts and minds," Kim writes. "Its political consequences are anything but trivial".

q5.stem: What do we learn from the passage about young Americans of today?
options: They have greater ambitions than their parents.
They find it difficult to achieve upward mobility.
They have overtaken their parents in terms of earnings.
They envy the opportunities in other industrialised nations.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「And yet, young Americans today are struggling to earn more than their parents did at the same age, and upward mobility in the US actually compares unfavourably to that of other industrialised nations.」
排除：A：未提野心更大，只述梦想强调野心。；C：未说收入超父母，反指难超同龄父母。；D：只比较流动性，未说羡慕他国机会。
q5.stemCn: 从文章中我们了解到当今美国年轻人什么？
optionsCn: 他们比父母有更大的雄心。
他们发现很难实现向上流动。
他们在收入方面已经超过了他们的父母。
他们羡慕其他工业化国家的机会。

q5.stem: What does Kim's team find about reality TV shows in America?
options: They reinterpret the essence of the popular rags-to-riches culture.
They urge people to achieve economic success through hard work.
They help strengthen people's conviction in the American Dream.
They feature ordinary Americans striving for social recognition.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream.」
排除：A：重述白手起家文化本质，无据；B：鼓励努力成功是节目剧情，非研究发现；D：提到普通人，但目标是经济成功，非社会认可
q5.stemCn: 金姆的团队对美国真人秀节目有什么发现？
optionsCn: 它们重新诠释了流行的白手起家文化的本质。
它们敦促人们通过努力工作取得经济成功。
它们有助于加强人们对美国梦的信念。
它们以追求社会认可的普通美国人为特色。

q5.stem: What does the author say about news broadcasts in America?
options: They attract far fewer viewers than reality TV.
They are bent on reporting the dark side of life.
They stand in striking contrast with reality TV.
They focus on Americans' economic hardships.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「And while these programmes are regularly among the most-watched shows, news broadcasts—which paint a more realistic view of the economic hardship faced by millions of Americans—get a much smaller proportion of the viewership.」
排除：A：B项“刻意渲染黑暗”无依据，原文只说更现实；B：C项“鲜明对照”无依据，原文只比较收视比例；C：D项“经济困难”只是新闻内容，非设问焦点。
q5.stemCn: 作者关于美国的新闻广播说了什么？
optionsCn: 它们的观众远比真人秀少。
它们致力于报道生活的阴暗面。
它们与真人秀形成鲜明对比。
它们关注美国人的经济困难。

q5.stem: What can we infer from the passage about Republicans in general?
options: They believe strongly in the American Dream.
They strive to climb the socio-economic ladder.
They have a very strong affiliation with their party.
They tend to watch more rags-to-riches TV shows.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「The results showed that those who'd watched a rags-to-riches clip did indeed have a significantly greater belief in the American Dream. Interestingly, when participants were separated by party affiliation, this effect was significant among Republicans but not Democrats, suggesting that the kind of messages implicit in these TV shows may play into people's existing socioeconomic beliefs.」
排除：B：原文未提及共和党更常看节目或更关注信念；C：原文未说共和党支持或反对反不平等政策；D：原文未说共和党完全否认向上流动
q5.stemCn: 从文章中我们可以推断出共和党人的一般情况是什么？
optionsCn: 他们坚信美国梦。
他们努力攀登社会经济阶梯。
他们对自己的政党有很强的归属感。
他们倾向于观看更多的白手起家的电视节目。

q5.stem: What is stated about people who believe in upward mobility?
options: They are likely to blame the government for their plight.
They regard political consequences as anything but trivial.
They respect individuals striving to climb the social ladder.
They are less likely to approve of policies to fight inequality.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「And here's the problem: if people mistakenly believe that hard work is all that is needed for individuals to make a better life for themselves, they may be less supportive of policies that could actually combat inequality.」
排除：A：未说他们会更支持相关政策。；B：未说该信念能缓解经济困难。；C：未说该信念仅来自现实节目。
q5.stemCn: 关于相信向上流动的人，文章陈述了什么？
optionsCn: 他们很可能因为自己的困境而指责政府。
他们认为政治后果绝非微不足道。
他们尊重那些努力攀登社会阶梯的个人。
他们不太可能赞成对抗不平等的政策。

items.cn:
“美国梦”承诺，在这个机遇之地，任何个人仅凭努力工作和雄心壮志就能攀爬经济阶梯并实现繁荣。然而，当今的美国年轻人发现，他们在同龄时赚的钱甚至不如父母当年多，而美国的向上流动性实际上与其他工业化国家相比处于劣势。
那么，为什么“美国梦”的理念依然经久不衰？《美国政治科学期刊》上的一项新研究指出一个被忽视的因素：真人秀的影响。
范德堡大学的恩智·金（Eunji Kim）指出，过去20年间，真人秀节目已主导了美国电视界。绝大多数这类节目都有“白手起家”的故事线：讲述普通美国人如何通过辛勤工作取得巨大的经济成功。虽然这些节目经常位居收视率榜首，但描绘数百万美国人面临的经济困境的更现实的新闻广播却只占很小的收视比例。
“白手起家”的故事在电视上无处不在——但观看这些节目真的能让人相信经济流动是容易实现的吗？为了找出答案，金的研究团队让参与者观看一段具有“白手起家”故事线的真人秀片段。对照组参与者则观看了一段没有“白手起家”故事的真人秀片段。观看节目后，参与者对四句与“美国梦”相关的陈述表达了同意程度。
结果显示，那些观看了“白手起家”片段的参与者确实对“美国梦”有着显著更强的信念。有趣的是，当按政党归属划分参与者时，这种效应在共和党人中显著，但在民主党人中并不显著，这表明这些电视节目中隐含的信息可能与人们现有的社会经济观念相契合。
金还对3000名美国居民进行了一项调查。他们也评估了自己认为生活成功与各种内部因素（如野心）和外部因素（如家庭财富）的相关程度。最后，他们阅读了一份电视节目列表，并指出哪些是他们定期观看的。
重度或频繁观看“白手起家”节目的参与者比从未观看此类节目的人对“美国梦”有更强烈的信念。
金得出结论：“‘白手起家’娱乐媒体是一种重要的文化力量，它促进并延续了人们对向上流动的信仰。”问题在于：如果人们错误地认为仅仅通过努力工作个人就能过上更好的生活，他们可能就不会支持那些真正能够遏制不平等的政策。
金写道：“在这个选择的时代，娱乐媒体俘获了人心。”“其政治后果绝非微不足道。”

items.src: 2024年6月 六级真题第2套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2024年6月 六级真题第2套 · 第2篇
items.text:
When someone asks us 'what do you do?' we nearly always reply with our occupation. Work, for many of us, is much more than a job. It is the defining aspect of our identity. For many of us it is through our job that we can define ourselves.
"Without my job I don't know who I am," is a sentence that has been uttered on more than a handful of occasions from my office chair. Indeed, it can be one of the most challenging aspects I work on with clients who have lost or been forced into changing their jobs. This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.
One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance. If we take the time to reflect we might recognise that as well as our work we can also identify as a friend, a spouse, a son or daughter, a parent, a member of a sports team or religious community. We may recognise that we feel and act differently in these roles and relationships than we do at work. The passive daughter becomes an assertive leader at work. Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time. I myself have been a shop assistant, a waitress, a student, a graduate, and a clinical psychologist. At each stage my ability to adapt to and develop my career identity has been crucial to my wellbeing. Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.
How we see ourselves is central to the issue of our identity. When we tell ourselves "I'm good at starting projects but not so great at seeing them through" it can become part of our belief system. But if you have the unfortunate experience of an enforced job change you will need to examine those beliefs to see how grounded in reality they are. You will be required to ask yourself how helpful these beliefs are and consider personal change. We can change our beliefs, behaviours and emotional experience at any time through experimentation, practice and conscious self-discipline. In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options. Ultimately it is you who define who you are. You are only your job if you let it be so.

q5.stem: What do we learn from the passage about one's loss of a job?
options: It compels them to visit a clinical psychologist.
It offers them a chance to play different roles.
It renders them puzzled about who they are.
It forces them to redefine their life's goals.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「This loss provokes an identity crisis much greater than the loss of the job itself.」
排除：A：未说经济困难；B：未说政策支持；C：正确，无需排除；D：未说亲友定义。
q5.stemCn: 从文章中我们了解到关于一个人失业的什么信息？
optionsCn: 它迫使他们去咨询临床心理学家。
它为他们提供了扮演不同角色的机会。
这让他们对自己是谁感到困惑。
它迫使他们重新定义人生目标。

q5.stem: What has the author come to understand about our identity?
options: It is crucial to our emotional wellbeing.
It plays a big role in many facets of life.
It reflects our changing status in society.
It is more complicated than it appears.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「One of the things I have come to understand, however, is that our identity is much more complex than we recognise at first glance.」
排除：A：原文说适应职业身份关乎幸福，非身份决定情绪；B：原文列多种身份，未说其在生活各方面起大作用；C：原文说工作身份会变，未说反映社会地位变化。
q5.stemCn: 作者对我们的身份认同有了什么理解？
optionsCn: 它对我们的情感健康至关重要。
它在生活的许多方面都起着重要作用。
它反映了我们在社会中不断变化的地位。
它比表面上看起来更复杂。

q5.stem: What does the passage say about our identities at work?
options: They are essential to our self-esteem.
They evolve with the passage of time.
They overrule all other self-perceptions.
They are key to understanding ourselves.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Furthermore, our identities at work are not static. They change over time.」
排除：A：原文说工作定义身份，但未称工作身份是自尊核心；C：原文未说工作身份压倒其他身份，反而列举多重角色；D：原文强调身份复杂，工作并非理解自我的唯一关键。
q5.stemCn: 文章关于我们在工作中的身份说了什么？
optionsCn: 它们对自尊心至关重要。
它们随着时间的推移而演变。
它们压倒所有其他的自我认知。
它们是理解我们自己的关键。

q5.stem: What do we have to do in today's ever-changing job market?
options: Strive to develop our social identity.
Prepare for different career paths.
Try to be assertive at all times.
Learn to manage uncertainty.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Whilst we like to eliminate uncertainty in our lives at some level we have to manage uncertainty, especially in today's volatile and ever-shifting job market.」
排除：A：文章未要求发展社会身份，只说明身份多样。；B：职业变化是背景，核心是管理不确定而非规划路径。；C：assertive 只是角色反差，并非要求时刻果断。
q5.stemCn: 在当今不断变化的就业市场中，我们必须做什么？
optionsCn: 努力发展我们的社会身份。
为不同的职业道路做好准备。
尝试在任何时候都保持自信坚定。
学会管理不确定性。

q5.stem: What should we do to expand our career options?
options: Alter our perceptions of ourselves.
Compare various job opportunities.
Look into newly emerging sectors.
Exercise self-discipline consciously.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「In an age where career progression may lead us into new sectors it is ever more important to challenge our sense of self and explore whether you can create a new experience of your identity by changing the beliefs you hold about yourself in order to expand your career options.」
排除：B：未提比较岗位机会，偏离身份与自我信念。；C：新部门只是背景，应对关键仍是改变自我信念。；D：自律仅是改变途径之一，题干强调自我认知。
q5.stemCn: 我们应该做什么来扩大职业选择？
optionsCn: 改变我们对自我的看法。
比较各种工作机会。
研究新兴行业。
自觉地锻炼自律能力。

items.cn:
当有人问我们“你是做什么的？”时，我们几乎总是回答自己的职业。对我们中的许多人来说，工作不仅仅是一份职位。它是界定我们身份的核心方面。对许多人而言，正是通过工作我们才能定义自己。
“没有我的工作，我不知道我是谁”，这句话在我办公室的椅子上已被多次听到。事实上，对于失去工作或被迫更换工作的客户来说，处理由此引发的危机是我工作中最具挑战性的方面之一。这种丧失感引发的身份危机远比失去工作本身带来的冲击更大。
然而，我逐渐认识到的一点是，我们的身份远比初看之下复杂得多。如果我们花时间反思，可能会意识到除了工作之外，我们还可以认同为朋友、配偶、儿子或女儿、父母、运动队成员或宗教社区成员。我们可能会发现，在这些角色和关系中，我们的感受和行为方式与在工作中不同。被动的“女儿”在工作中可能成为果断的领导者。此外，我们在职业上的身份并非静止不变的，它们会随时间变化。我自己曾做过店员、服务员、学生、毕业生和临床心理学家。在每个阶段，适应和发展我的职业身份的能力对我的幸福感至关重要。虽然我们喜欢在某种程度上消除生活中的不确定性，但我们必须管理不确定性，尤其是在当今动荡且不断变化的就业市场中。
如何看待自己是身份问题的核心。当我们告诉自己“我擅长开启项目，但不善于坚持到底”时，这可能会成为我们信念体系的一部分。但如果你不幸经历了被迫换工作的情况，你需要审视这些信念有多少现实依据。你将需要询问自己这些信念是否有帮助，并考虑做出个人改变。我们可以通过实验、练习和有意识的自我约束随时改变我们的信念、行为和情感体验。在一个职业发展可能引领我们进入新领域的时代，挑战我们的自我认知变得愈发重要，探索是否可以通过改变对自己的信念来创造新的身份体验，从而拓宽你的职业选择。最终，是你自己定义了你是谁。只有当你允许工作定义你时，你才仅仅是你的工作。

items.title: 2024年6月 六级真题第3套 · 第1篇
items.text:
Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them. Sarcasm is mostly understood through tone of voice, which is used to portray the opposite of the literal words. For example, when someone says, "Well, that's exactly what I need right now," their tone can tell you it's not what they need at all.
Most frequently, sarcasm highlights an irritation or is, quite simply, mean.
If you want to be happier and improve your relationships, cut out sarcasm. Why? Because sarcasm is actually hostility disguised as humor.
Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible. Indeed, it's not surprising that the origin of the word sarcasm derives from the Greek word "sarkazein" which literally means "to tear or strip the flesh off." Hence, it's no wonder that sarcasm is often preceded by the word "cutting" and that it hurts.
What's more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity. After all, when you come right down to it, sarcasm can be used as a subtle form of bullying—and most bullies are angry, insecure, or cowardly.
Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.
Now, I'm not saying all sarcasm is bad. It may just be better used sparingly—like a potent spice in cooking. Too much of the spice, and the dish will be overwhelmed by it. Similarly, an occasional dash of sarcastic wit can spice up a chat and add an element of humor to it. But a big or steady serving of sarcasm will overwhelm the emotional flavor of any conversation and can taste very bitter to its recipient.
So, tone down the sarcasm and work on clever wit instead, which is usually without any hostility and thus more appreciated by those you're communicating with. In essence, sarcasm is easy while true, harmless wit takes talent.
Thus, the main difference between wit and sarcasm is that, as already stated, sarcasm is often hostility disguised as humor. It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities. Sarcastic statements are expressed in a cutting manner; witty remarks are delivered with undisguised and harmless humor.

q5.stem: Why does the author say sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common?
options: Both are recognized when heard.
Both have exactly the same tone.
Both mean the opposite of what they appear to.
Both have hidden in them an evident irritation.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Sarcasm and jazz have something surprisingly in common: You know them when you hear them.」
排除：B：原文未说两者语气相同；C：反义仅针对讽刺，非爵士；D：烦躁只属讽刺，未提爵士
q5.stemCn: 作者为什么说讽刺和爵士乐有着出人意料的共同点？
optionsCn: 两者在听到时都能被识别。
两者具有完全相同的音调。
两者都意味着与其表面看似相反的意思。
两者都隐藏着明显的恼怒。

q5.stem: How do many people feel when they hear sarcastic comments?
options: They feel hostile towards the sarcastic person.
They feel belittled and disrespected.
They feel a strong urge to retaliate.
They feel incapable of disguising their irritation.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Despite smiling outwardly, many people who receive sarcastic comments feel put down and often think the sarcastic person is rude, or contemptible.」
排除：A：原文未说接收者产生敌意；C：原文未提强烈报复冲动；D：原文未说无法掩饰恼怒
q5.stemCn: 当人们听到讽刺性的评论时，他们会有什么感觉？
optionsCn: 他们对说讽刺话的人感到敌意。
他们感到被贬低和不被尊重。
他们感到强烈的报复冲动。
他们觉得无法掩饰自己的恼怒。

q5.stem: What happens when a person consistently acts sarcastically?
options: They feel their dignity greatly heightened.
They feel increasingly insecure and hostile.
They endure hostility under the disguise of humor.
They taste bitterness even in pleasant interactions.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「What's more, since actions strongly determine thoughts and feelings, when a person consistently acts sarcastically it may only serve to heighten their underlying hostility and insecurity.」
排除：A：原文说增强敌意与不安，不是尊严提升；C：受伤害的是听者，非惯用讽刺者自身；D：苦涩是受话人感受，非自身愉悦互动变苦
q5.stemCn: 当一个人持续表现出自以为是或讽刺的态度时会发生什么？
optionsCn: 他们觉得自己的尊严大大提升。
他们感到越来越不安全且充满敌意。
他们在幽默的伪装下忍受着敌意。
即使在愉快的互动中，他们也尝到了苦涩。

q5.stem: What does the author say about people quitting sarcastic comments?
options: It makes others happier and more self-confident.
It restrains them from being irritating and bullying.
It benefits not only themselves but also those around them.
It shields them from negative comments and outright hostility.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Alternatively, when a person stops voicing negative comments, especially sarcastic ones, they may soon start to feel happier and more self-confident. Also, other people in their life benefit even more because they no longer have to hear the emotionally hurtful language of sarcasm.」
排除：A：原文未说只让他人幸福，自己也受益；B：原文未称戒讽刺能抑制欺凌；D：重点是不再说讽刺，而非躲避敌意。
q5.stemCn: 关于人们停止发表讽刺性评论，作者说了什么？
optionsCn: 这让其他人更快乐、更自信。
这阻止了他们变得令人讨厌和霸凌他人。
这不仅对他们自己有益，也对周围的人有益。
这保护他们免受负面评论和公然敌意的伤害。

q5.stem: What is the chief difference between a speaker's wit and sarcasm?
options: Their clarity.
Their appreciation.
Their emphasis.
Their intention.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「It can be intended to hurt and is often bitter and biting. Witty statements are usually in response to someone's unhelpful remarks or behaviors, and the intent is to untangle and clarify the issue by emphasizing its absurdities.」
排除：A：清晰只是幽默目的，非讽刺与机智主要区别；B：受欢迎程度非原文区分讽刺与机智的标准；C：强调荒谬是机智的表达方式，非本质差异
q5.stemCn: 说话者的机智（wit）与讽刺（sarcasm）之间的主要区别是什么？
optionsCn: 它们的清晰度。
它们的欣赏程度。
它们的侧重点。
它们的意图。

items.cn:
讽刺和爵士乐有一个惊人的共同点：当你听到它们时，你立刻就能识别出来。讽刺主要通过语调来传达，这种语调用来表达与字面意思相反的含义。例如，当有人说“嗯，这正是我现在需要的”时，他们的语气却能告诉你这根本不是他们想要的。
讽刺最常用来突显一种恼怒情绪，或者简单来说，就是刻薄。
如果你想更快乐并改善人际关系，请戒掉讽刺。为什么？因为讽刺实际上是伪装成幽默的敌意。
尽管表面上在微笑，许多收到讽刺评论的人却感到被贬低，并且常常认为讽刺者粗鲁或令人鄙视。确实，讽刺一词源自希腊语“sarkazein”，其字面意思是“撕裂或剥去肉皮”，因此它的起源并不令人意外。所以，讽刺常与“尖锐（cutting）”一词连用也就不足为奇了，而且它确实伤人。
此外，既然行为强烈地决定了思想和感受，当一个人持续表现讽刺时，这可能只会加剧他们潜藏的敌意和不安全感。毕竟，说到底，讽刺可以被用作一种微妙的欺凌形式——而大多数欺凌者都是愤怒、缺乏安全感或懦弱的。
反之，当一个人停止发表负面评论，尤其是讽刺性的评论时，他们可能很快会开始感觉更快乐、更自信。此外，他们生活中的其他人也会受益更多，因为他们不必再听到那些情感上伤人的讽刺语言。
现在，我并不是说所有的讽刺都是坏的。也许最好只是适度使用——就像烹饪中的一种强力香料一样。香料放得太多，菜肴会被其味道掩盖。同样，偶尔一点机智的讽刺可以为聊天增添风味并增加幽默元素。但是，大量或持续的讽刺会使任何对话的情感基调变得沉重，对接受者来说滋味可能非常苦涩。
因此，收敛你的讽刺，转而培养机智的幽默感，后者通常不带任何敌意，因此更容易被与你交流的人所欣赏。本质上，讽刺很容易做到，而真正无害的机智则需要才华。
因此，机智与讽刺的主要区别在于，正如前文所述，讽刺通常是伪装成幽默的敌意。它可能意在伤害，往往尖酸刻薄。机智的话语通常是对某人无益言论或行为的回应，其意图是通过强调荒谬之处来理清和澄清问题。讽刺的表达方式是尖锐刺耳的；而机智的话语则以不加掩饰且无害的幽默方式呈现。

items.title: 2024年6月 六级真题第3套 · 第2篇
items.text:
Variability is crucially important for learning new skills. Consider learning how to serve in tennis. Should you always practise serving from the exactly same location on the court, aiming at the same spot? Although practising in more variable conditions will be slower at first, it will likely make you a better tennis player in the end. This is because variability leads to better generalisation of what is learned.
This principle is found in many domains, including speech perception and learning categories. For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.
"There are over ten different names for this basic principle," says Limor Raviv, the senior investigator of a recent study. "Learning from less variable input is often fast, but may fail to generalise to new stimuli."
To identify key patterns and understand the underlying principles of variability effects, Raviv and her colleagues reviewed over 150 studies on variability and generalisation across fields, including computer science, linguistics, categorisation, visual perception and formal education.
The researchers discovered that, across studies, the term variability can refer to at least four different kinds of variability, such as set size and scheduling. "These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.
The impact of variability depends on whether it is relevant to the task or not. But according to the 'Mr. Miyagi principle', practising seemingly unrelated skills may actually benefit learning of other skills.
But why does variability impact learning and generalisation? One theory is that more variable input can highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not.
Another theory is that greater variability leads to broader generalisations. This is because variability will represent the real world better, including atypical(非典型的) examples.
A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.
"Understanding the impact of variability is important for literally every aspect of our daily life. Beyond affecting the way we learn language, motor skills, and categories, it even has an impact on our social lives," explains Raviv. "For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community. Exposure to fewer faces during childhood is associated with diminished face memory."
"We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv. "Our paper raises a lot of open questions. Can we find similar effects of variability beyond the brain, for instance, in the immune system?"

q5.stem: What does the passage say about infants learning the category "dog" if they are exposed to Chihuahuas only?
options: They will encounter some degree of difficulty.
They will try to categorise other objects first.
They will prefer Chihuahuas to other dog species.
They will imagine Chihuahuas in various conditions.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「For instance, infants will struggle to learn the category "dog" if they are only exposed to Chihuahuas, instead of many different kinds of dogs.」
排除：B：未提先分类其他；C：未提偏爱吉娃娃；D：未提想象不同情况。
q5.stemCn: 如果婴儿只接触过吉娃娃犬，文章关于他们学习“狗”这一类别的说法是什么？
optionsCn: 他们会遇到一定程度的困难。
他们会先尝试对其他物体进行分类。
他们会更喜欢吉娃娃而不是其他品种的狗。
他们会想象各种状态下的吉娃娃。

q5.stem: What does Raviv say about the four different kinds of variability?
options: Which of them is most relevant to the task at hand is to be confirmed.
Why they have an impact on learning is far from being understood.
Why they have never been directly compared remains a mystery.
Which of them is most conducive to learning is yet to be identified.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「"These four kinds of variability have never been directly compared—which means that we currently don't know which is most effective for learning," says Raviv.」
排除：A：原文未谈确认哪种与任务最相关；B：文章已解释影响原因，非未理解；C：原文指未比较，未问为何未比较
q5.stemCn: 拉维夫（Raviv）关于四种不同的变异性类型说了什么？
optionsCn: 哪一种与当前任务最相关尚待确认。
它们为何影响学习还远未被理解。
它们为何从未被直接比较仍是一个谜。
哪一种最有利于学习尚未确定。

q5.stem: How does one of the theories explain the importance of variability for learning new skills?
options: Learners regard variable training as typical of what happens in the real world.
Learners receiving variable training are compelled to reorganise their memories.
Learners pay attention to the relevant aspects of a task and ignore those irrelevant.
Learners focus on related skills instead of wasting time and effort on unrelated ones.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「A third reason has to do with the way memory works: when training is variable, learners are forced to actively reconstruct their memories.」
排除：A：属第一理论，强调识别相关方面；C：属第二理论，强调泛化；D：变异性初期通常更慢。
q5.stemCn: 其中一种理论如何解释变异性对于学习新技能的重要性？
optionsCn: 学习者将多变量的训练视为现实世界中典型情况。
接受多变量训练的学习者被迫重组他们的记忆。
学习者关注任务的相关方面并忽略无关方面。
学习者专注于相关技能，而不是浪费时间和精力在不相关的技能上。

q5.stem: What does the passage say about face recognition?
options: People growing up in a small community may find it easy to remember familiar faces.
Face recognition has a significant impact on literally every aspect of our social lives.
People growing up in a large community can readily recognise any individual faces.
The size of the community people grow up in impacts their face recognition ability.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「For example, face recognition is affected by whether people grew up in a small community or in a larger community.」
排除：A：小社区会削弱记忆，并非更易认脸；B：是变异影响日常，非面部识别影响所有社交生活；C：未说大社区可轻易识别任何个体面孔
q5.stemCn: 关于人脸识别，文章说了什么？
optionsCn: 在小社区长大的人可能发现记住熟悉的面孔很容易。
人脸识别对我们社会生活的几乎每一个方面都有重大影响。
在大社区长大的人可以轻易识别任何个人的面孔。
人们成长社区的规模影响了他们的人脸识别能力。

q5.stem: What does Raviv hope to do with their research work?
options: Highlight which aspects of a task are relevant and which are not to learning a skill.
Use the principle of variability in teaching seemingly unrelated skills in education.
Arouse people's interest in variability and stimulate more research on the topic.
Apply the principle of variability to such fields of study as the immune system.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「"We hope this work will spark people's curiosity and generate more work on the topic," concludes Raviv.」
排除：A：属理论解释，非研究希望；B：未提用于教学，属无关推断；D：仅开放问题，非直接希望。
q5.stemCn: 拉维夫希望用他们的研究工作做什么？
optionsCn: 强调任务的哪些方面与学习技能相关，哪些不相关。
在教育中利用变异性原理教授看似无关的技能。
唤起人们对变异性的兴趣并刺激更多相关研究。
将变异性原理应用于免疫系统等领域。

items.cn:
可变性对于学习新技能至关重要。以学习网球发球为例。你应该总是从球场上完全相同的位置练习发球，瞄准同一个点吗？虽然在更多样化的条件下练习起初会更慢，但最终它可能会让你成为一名更好的网球运动员。这是因为可变性能带来所学内容更好的泛化能力。
这一原理在许多领域都能找到，包括语音感知和类别学习。例如，如果婴儿只接触吉娃娃，而不是各种不同类型的狗，他们将难以学习“狗”这个类别。
“这一基本原理有十多种不同的名称，”近期一项研究的首席研究员利莫尔·拉维夫（Limor Raviv）说。“从较少变化的输入中学习通常很快，但可能无法泛化到新的刺激。”
为了识别关键模式并理解可变性效应背后的基本原理，拉维夫及其同事回顾了跨越多个领域的150多项关于可变性和泛化的研究，包括计算机科学、语言学、分类学、视觉感知和正规教育。
研究人员发现，在各项研究中，“可变性”一词至少可以指代四种不同类型的可变性，如集合大小和时间安排。“这四种类型的可变性从未被直接比较过——这意味着我们目前不知道哪一种对学习最有效，”拉维夫说。
可变性的影响取决于它是否与任务相关。但根据‘宫城先生原则’，练习看似无关的技能实际上可能有利于其他技能的学习。
那么，为什么可变性会影响学习和泛化呢？一种理论认为，更多样的输入可以突出任务的哪些方面是相关的，哪些是不相关的。
另一种理论认为，更大的可变性会导致更广泛的泛化。这是因为可变性更好地代表了现实世界，包括非典型的例子。
第三个原因与记忆的工作方式有关：当训练具有可变性时，学习者被迫主动重构他们的记忆。
“理解可变性的影响对我们日常生活的方方面面都至关重要。除了影响我们学习语言、运动技能和分类的方式外，它甚至对我们的社交生活也有影响，”拉维夫解释道。“例如，人脸识别受到人们是在小社区还是大社区长大的影响。童年时期接触较少的面孔与面部记忆减退有关。”
“我们希望这项工作能激发人们的好奇心，并催生更多关于该主题的研究，”拉维夫总结道。“我们的论文提出了许多未解决的问题。我们能否在大脑之外发现类似的可变性效应？”

items.title: 2024年12月 六级真题第1套 · 第1篇
items.text:
Imagine you're an alien sent to Earth to document the behaviour of the mammals inhabiting the planet. You stumble into a movie theatre that's showing the latest Hollywood horror film.
Several dozen humans are gathered together in a dark, undecorated room. They're all staring at a rectangular area on which patterns of light change rapidly.
They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.
Eventually, the lights come up and the rectangular screen goes black. The humans stand up and leave the room, chatting and laughing, and showing signs of pleasure.
Why do these humans voluntarily expose themselves to what appears to be a deeply unpleasant experience? And why do they react so strongly to those patterns of light on a screen?
I am fascinated with the paradox of horror—the strange fact that many people seek out scary entertainment.
I think the answer to the puzzle lies in human nature.
My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context. You can see these elements of horror in children's games. Take hide-and-seek for example, which is a simulation of a predator-prey interaction. The kid hides and the adult pretends to be a predator, searching for the child while howling like a dangerous beast.
This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.
They find it pleasurable, and pleasure is evolution's way of motivating us toward adaptive behaviour.
Horror is pleasurable to many people because it lets us play with negative emotions and develop coping strategies. We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.
How, then, does horror work? My research suggests that horror works by exploiting an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms—an evolved fear system, which we share with other animals. But humans are uniquely imaginative, and we use our evolved imagination to travel into virtual worlds that are full of danger.
There are good reasons for watching a horror film, even if you're not a loyal horror fan. If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience. Anyway, watching a horror film makes you better at handling your own fear, and who knows when that will become critically relevant?

q5.stem: The alien finds the audience in the movie theatre clearly in a state of ______.
options: total mindfulness
extreme excitement
spiritual elevation
intense curiosity
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「They are clearly in a state of high arousal. Their heart rate is elevated, they occasionally glance around nervously, and they sometimes jump collectively in their seats, and emit high-pitched warning calls.」
排除：A：文中说高度唤醒，并非正念；C：紧张和惊叫属生理反应，非精神升华；D：被吓出反应，非单纯强烈好奇
q5.stemCn: 外星人发现电影院里的观众显然处于______状态。
optionsCn: 完全正念的状态
极度兴奋的状态
精神升华的状态
强烈好奇的状态

q5.stem: Why do many people seek out scary entertainment, according to the author's research?
options: They gain experience in overcoming horror in real life.
They find joy in going through simulated horrible experiences.
They have learned from hide-and-seek as kids the thrill involved.
They have evolved to gain pleasure in escaping life-threatening situations.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「My research suggests that we humans evolved to find pleasure in situations that allow us to experience negative emotions in a safe context.」
排除：A：原文指安全情境中体验恐惧，并非真实生活中克服恐怖；C：hide-and-seek仅是儿童游戏举例，非寻求恐怖娱乐的原因；D：原文指安全情境中体验负面情绪，非真正逃离生命威胁。
q5.stemCn: 根据作者的研究，为什么许多人寻求恐怖娱乐？
optionsCn: 他们获得了在现实生活中克服恐惧的经验。
他们在经历模拟的可怕体验中找到了乐趣。
他们从小时候玩捉迷藏中学到了其中的刺激感。
他们进化出了从逃离危及生命的情境中获得快感的能力。

q5.stem: What do children learn from hide-and-seek?
options: How to avoid falling prey to an attacker.
How to simulate a predator-prey interaction.
How to keep themselves from catastrophic errors.
How to turn a dangerous scenario into a safe one.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「This simulation gives the child crucial information about how to avoid becoming prey, and children tend to find that kind of activity deeply satisfying, presumably because it gives them a safe experience of a potentially catastrophic scenario.」
排除：B：模拟互动是游戏性质，不是孩子所学。；C：原文强调避免成猎物，非防灾难错误。；D：活动提供安全体验，非孩子转化危险。
q5.stemCn: 孩子们从捉迷藏中学到了什么？
optionsCn: 如何避免成为攻击者的猎物。
如何模拟捕食者与猎物的互动。
如何防止自己犯下灾难性的错误。
如何将危险场景转化为安全场景。

q5.stem: Why is horror gratifying to many people?
options: It reminds them of an ancient set of biological defence mechanisms.
It triggers their imagination to travel into dangerous virtual worlds.
It allows them to learn what fear feels like and how to tackle it.
It activates their evolved fear system and their unique fantasy.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「We learn what it feels like to be truly afraid, and we learn how to handle negative emotion.」
排除：A：只是机制，未答令人愉悦原因；B：想象危险，非直接愉悦原因；D：唤醒恐惧系统，未说明愉悦
q5.stemCn: 为什么恐怖对许多人来说是一种满足？
optionsCn: 它让他们想起一套古老的生物防御机制。
它激发他们的想象力去探索危险的虚拟世界。
它让他们了解恐惧的感觉以及如何应对恐惧。
它激活了他们进化而来的恐惧系统和独特的幻想。

q5.stem: What will one experience if they watch a horror film through without being hurt?
options: A strong sense of clear relevance.
A profound sense of good fortune.
A profound sense of intense relief.
A strong sense of being in control.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「If you make it through the film in one piece, you'll probably experience a strong sense of mastery, a sense that you were able to make it through an appalling experience.」
排除：A：原文未提观影后有明确相关性之感；B：原文未提及劫后余生的幸运感；C：原文强调掌控感，非强烈解脱感
q5.stemCn: 如果一个人观看恐怖片时毫发无伤地看完，他们会体验到什么？
optionsCn: 一种强烈的明确关联感。
一种深刻的幸运感。
一种深刻的强烈如释重负感。
一种强烈的掌控感。

items.cn:
想象你是一个被派往地球记录该星球上哺乳动物行为的外星人。你偶然走进一家正在放映最新好莱坞恐怖片的电影院。
几十个人聚集在一个黑暗、毫无装饰的房间里。他们都盯着一个矩形区域，那里的光影图案变化迅速。
他们显然处于高度兴奋状态。他们的心率加快，偶尔紧张地环顾四周，有时还会集体从座位上跳起来，发出尖利的警告声。
最终，灯光亮起，矩形屏幕变黑。人们站起来离开房间，有说有笑，流露出愉悦的迹象。
为什么这些人类自愿将自己暴露在这种看似极度不愉快的体验中？为什么他们对屏幕上那些光影图案的反应如此强烈？
我对恐怖悖论着迷——许多人寻求惊悚娱乐这一奇怪事实。
我认为这个谜题的答案在于人性。
我的研究表明，我们人类进化出了一种能力，即在安全的情境下体验负面情绪并从中获得快感。你可以在儿童游戏中看到这些恐怖元素。以捉迷藏为例，这是一种捕食者与猎物互动的模拟。孩子躲起来，大人假装成捕食者，一边像危险的野兽一样嚎叫，一边寻找孩子。
这种模拟给了孩子关于如何避免成为猎物的关键信息，孩子们往往觉得这类活动令人深深满足，这大概是因为它让他们在安全的体验中经历了潜在的灾难性场景。
他们觉得这很快乐，而快乐是进化激励我们采取适应性行为的方式。
恐怖对许多人来说是愉快的，因为它让我们能够玩弄负面情绪并发展应对策略。我们学习真正感到恐惧是什么滋味，也学习如何处理负面情绪。
那么，恐怖是如何起作用的呢？我的研究表明，恐怖通过利用一套古老的生物防御机制——一个与其他动物共享的进化而来的恐惧系统——来发挥作用。但人类拥有独特的想象力，我们利用进化来的想象力进入充满危险的虚拟世界。
即使你不是忠实的恐怖片粉丝，观看恐怖片也有充分的理由。如果你能毫发无损地看完电影，你可能会体验到一种强烈的掌控感，一种你能熬过可怕经历的成就感。无论如何，看恐怖片能让你更擅长处理自己的恐惧，谁知道什么时候这种能力会变得至关重要呢？

items.src: 2024年12月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2024年12月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.text:
An awakening has been taking place in the physical world against the beauty model that has been dictated to us for years. But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.
The two opposing struggles are taking place in parallel. In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal. As part of the struggle, various media outlets have presented women whose bodies don't correspond to the so-called ideal. All those women who had previously been excluded from the covers of magazines, television series and the public agenda, have become "legitimate". At the same time, a group of influencers have begun to upload to social media photos of themselves without makeup, and even photos in which they highlight supposed flaws.
Technology has reshaped our beauty ideal and is doing a great job communicating that message to the masses. One of the bizarre legacies of the past decade is the popularity of the "cyborg look", which illustrates what Americans will look like in 2050.
The cyborg look spread rapidly. Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.
The internalization of accepted beauty norms is much more effective when there is active involvement in the learning process. The active involvement of users is reflected in the gamified(游戏化的) interaction offered by the social media platforms—the ability to like, write a comment, compare, share.
Once the desired beauty ideal has been internalized, users are given tools or features to change their appearance to suit the accepted beauty ideal such as editing the image, choosing the ideal filter, the right background.
A survey conducted in the United States revealed that more than 50% filter the images before posting them. And you will not be surprised to hear that the majority of them are women. One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.
The effect of the filters is already far beyond amiable amusement. The filters and the entire game played on the networks affect the mental health of the users. According to a study, apps like Instagram, Snapchat and FaceTune allow users to achieve a level of perfection that was previously only observed in beauty magazines.
Even though humanity has always cherished beauty, in the last decade our obsession with looks has reached an unprecedented peak. The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.

q5.stem: What do we learn about beauty in the digital arena?
options: It dictates the taste of digital media.
It has been in the making for years.
It has ushered in a new awakening.
It is defined by social media.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「But in the digital arena, social media determines what is considered beautiful.」
排除：A：美不左右数字品味，而是社媒定审美；B：觉醒在现实世界，非数字领域；C：数字领域由社媒定美，非既定理想
q5.stemCn: 关于数字领域的美，我们了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它主导了数字媒体的品味。
它多年来一直在形成中。
它开启了新的觉醒时代。
它由社交媒体定义。

q5.stem: What does the passage say about beauty in the physical world?
options: Women are under constant pressure to keep up with beauty models.
Women are encouraged to pursue a beauty ideal that has never existed.
A fight is going on to remove pressure on women to conform to an absurd beauty ideal.
Media outlets have begun to present as beauty models trendy women without any makeup.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「In the physical world, the struggle goes against the underlying pressure exerted on women to conform to an unrealistic beauty ideal.」
排除：A：原文指反对迫使女性迎合不切实际的美，未说女性应紧跟美模。；B：文中称理想不切实际，未说该美从未存在。；D：媒体展示不符理想的女性，未说无妆者成时尚美模。
q5.stemCn: 关于物理世界中的美，文章说了什么？
optionsCn: 女性面临着跟上审美标准的持续压力。
女性被鼓励追求一种从未存在过的理想美。
正在进行一场消除迫使女性顺应荒谬审美理想的压力的斗争。
媒体开始将不化妆的时尚女性作为审美榜样呈现。

q5.stem: What do we learn from the passage about the Instagram face?
options: It is now regarded as the new beauty ideal.
It is what most women will go after in 2050.
It is being much talked about on social media.
It is a perfect illustration of the ultimate beauty.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Today, however, the Instagram face has become the new beauty ideal.」
排除：B：原文把2050外貌指向cyborg look，非此。；C：原文未称它被多数人追随，属过度推断。；D：原文未说它代表完美，只是新审美标准。
q5.stemCn: 从文章中关于“Instagram脸”（网红脸），我们了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它现在被视为新的审美理想。
它是大多数女性在2050年将会追求的目标。
它在社交媒体上被大量讨论。
它是终极完美的完美例证。

q5.stem: What has obsessive filtering resulted in?
options: A good many women striving to reach an impossible level of perfection.
An urge to turn the entire game played on the network to one's advantage.
A tendency to regard one's body as an object of observation and judgment.
An increasing number of women filtering their images before uploading them.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「One of the significant consequences of obsessive filtering is the emerging tendency to treat oneself as an object to be observed and valued, in the same way another person observes and judges from the side.」
排除：A：原文未把A项说成过度过滤的直接后果；B：原文未说将网络博弈转为优势；D：女性常过滤是背景事实，非结果。
q5.stemCn: 强迫性滤镜导致了什么结果？
optionsCn: 许多女性努力达到不可能的完美水平。
一种将整个网络博弈变为对自己有利局面的冲动。
一种将自己的身体视为观察和评判对象的倾向。
越来越多的女性在上传图片前会对图像进行滤镜处理。

q5.stem: What does the author want to emphasize at the end of the passage regarding Americans' obsession with looks?
options: Cosmetic surgery should be made more accessible to the masses.
Psychological intervention should be introduced to alleviate it.
Their time spent on social media should be strictly controlled.
Its root cause should be meticulously examined and analyzed.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「The time spent on social media creates an urge to achieve an impossible beauty ideal so powerful that the only thing that can fix it is not cosmetic intervention, but mental health care.」
排除：A：文中称修复办法不是整容干预，而非让整容更普及；C：文章未主张严控使用时间，只说它催生冲动；D：重点为心理照护，并非追溯成因。
q5.stemCn: 在文章结尾，关于美国人对外表的痴迷，作者想强调什么？
optionsCn: 应该让大众更容易获得整容手术。
应引入心理干预以缓解这种痴迷。
应严格限制他们在社交媒体上花费的时间。
应仔细审视和分析其根本原因。

items.cn:
在现实世界中，一场反对多年来强加给我们的审美标准的觉醒运动正在进行。但在数字领域，社交媒体决定了什么是美。
这两场对立的斗争并行发生。在现实世界中，这场斗争旨在反抗施加在女性身上的、要求她们符合不切实际的审美理想的基础压力。作为这场斗争的一部分，各种媒体展示了身体不符合所谓“理想”的女性。所有以前被排除在杂志封面、电视剧集和公共议程之外的女性，都变得“合法化”了。与此同时，一群网红开始在社交媒体上上传自己素颜的照片，甚至是那些突出所谓缺陷的照片。
技术重塑了我们的审美理想，并在向大众传达这一信息方面做得非常出色。过去十年最奇怪的遗产之一就是“赛博格风格”的流行，它描绘了2050年美国人的模样。
赛博格风格迅速蔓延。然而如今，“Instagram脸”已成为新的审美理想。
当学习过程中有主动参与时，内化接受的美学规范会更有效。用户的主动参与体现在社交媒体平台提供的游戏化互动中——点赞、写评论、比较和分享的能力。
一旦期望的审美理想被内化，用户就会获得工具或功能来改变他们的外表，以适应接受的美学理想，例如编辑图像、选择理想的滤镜、合适的背景。
在美国进行的一项调查显示，超过50%的人在发布前会对图片进行滤镜处理。你不会惊讶地发现，其中大多数是女性。过度使用滤镜的一个重要后果是，出现了一种将自己视为被观察和被评估的对象的倾向，就像另一个人从旁边观察和评判那样。
滤镜的影响早已超越了友善的娱乐范畴。滤镜以及整个在网络平台上进行的这场游戏影响了用户的心理健康。根据一项研究，像Instagram、Snapchat和FaceTune这样的应用允许用户达到以前只在美容杂志上看到的那种完美水平。
尽管人类一直珍视美，但在过去的十年里，我们对容貌的痴迷达到了前所未有的顶峰。花在社交媒体上的时间产生了一种追求不可能实现的审美理想的冲动，这种冲动如此强大，以至于唯一能解决它的不是整容手术，而是心理健康护理。

items.src: 2024年12月 六级真题第2套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2024年12月 六级真题第2套 · 第1篇
items.text:
With population increases and global urbanisation ever accelerating, much attention is focused on the sustainability of our cities and scarce attention is paid to the countryside.
Rural life is associated with closely-knit communities, sense of belonging, and a simple, tranquil life. Yet whilst some or all of these elements exist in the countryside, so do conservatism and a lack of employment opportunities. And it is mostly due to the latter that rural communities are suffering. Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.
So how can the countryside ensure its survival among these changes; or should it at all? Due to both the distance between residences and facilities and often intermittent public transport, those living in the countryside are heavier automobile users. Rural dwellers also use more energy maintaining their mostly detached buildings. We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match. Rural energy requirements result in higher carbon emissions per person than in the city, so it is actually irresponsible to endorse such a lifestyle choice.
Protecting the countryside is a hot topic. Those who have made their fortunes in the city often buy second homes in the countryside, visiting intermittently for a sample of a supposedly simple life. The side-effect of this is that house prices are pushed up due to increased demand, leaving them unaffordable for local people. A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.
Whilst an idealised view of the countryside is common, the reality is that rural life has continuously evolved. Industrialisation brought an increase in divisions of labour, changing social links between rural people. The internet has introduced once foreign cultures into the countryside. Improved travel connections and affordability have made the world more accessible, creating a "global village". Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.
Perhaps the countryside should also prepare itself for massive population increases in the future. With cities across the world growing rapidly, how will the current urban generation respond to the inevitable social changes of mass urbanisation? Will the longing for a simpler life become stronger, fueling a rural renaissance?
As the world continues to urbanise, the voices calling for rural preservation may well grow louder. But change is inevitable. We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.

q5.stem: What has become of the rural areas nowadays?
options: They are becoming somewhat deserted.
They are being increasingly urbanised.
They are closely-knit communities.
They are haunted by conservatism.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Attracted by the improved economics of urban areas, country-dwellers across the world are moving out, contributing to the excessive crowdedness of densely populated cities, and leaving the countryside in desolation.」
排除：B：人口外流致城市拥挤，非乡村城市化。；C：紧密社区是乡村理想关联，非现状。；D：保守主义只是存在问题，非主要后果。
q5.stemCn: 如今农村地区的情况如何？
optionsCn: 它们正变得有些荒凉。
它们正在日益城市化。
它们是紧密相连的社区。
它们被保守主义所困扰。

q5.stem: What does the author think of the rural lifestyle?
options: It is unlikely to survive given the on-going changes.
It is less energy-efficient compared to that in cities.
It is highly dependent upon heavy automobiles.
It is a choice more affluent people will endorse.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「We may be piled up like boxes in the city, but this brings energy efficiency that the countryside cannot match.」
排除：A：未来只是不明朗，不等于难以存活；C：汽车只是耗能原因，非总体评价；D：文中未说富人普遍支持此选择。
q5.stemCn: 作者如何看待农村生活方式？
optionsCn: 鉴于持续的变化，它不太可能存续。
与城市相比，它的能源效率较低。
它高度依赖重型汽车。
这是更富裕人群会支持的选择。

q5.stem: What does the author think of rich urban residents buying a second home in the countryside?
options: It is bound to mar the traditional rural life.
It adversely impacts rural social stability.
It hinders rural economies' revitalisation.
It is detrimental to rural preservation.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「A solution has yet to be found for this challenge, for market forces are further forcing residents out of the countryside. For those who believe in rural preservation, this is deplorable.」
排除：A：原文未称其必然破坏传统乡村生活；B：未提及乡村社会稳定性受影响；C：未说其阻碍乡村经济复兴。
q5.stemCn: 作者如何看待富裕的城市居民在农村购买第二居所？
optionsCn: 这注定会破坏传统的农村生活。
它对农村社会稳定产生不利影响。
它阻碍了农村经济的振兴。
这对农村保护有害。

q5.stem: What do we learn about the countryside with industrialisation and technological advances?
options: It is destined to change gradually.
It will present an idealised way of life.
It is likely to embrace foreign cultures.
It will become increasingly diversified.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Considering these changes, surely an evolving countryside is inevitable.」
排除：B：原文说理想化看法常见，并非会呈现理想生活；C：仅说互联网引入外来文化，非题干结论；D：未说日益多样化，只说必然演变。
q5.stemCn: 关于工业化和科技进步下的乡村，我们了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它注定会逐渐改变。
它将呈现一种理想化的生活方式。
它可能会接纳外国文化。
它将变得越来越多样化。

q5.stem: What does the author think of the future of the countryside compared with cities?
options: It is going to be harder for the locals.
It is going to resemble that of cities.
It is less likely to stay static.
It is less easy to envisage.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「We know that the world is going to see new cities emerging from the dust and current cities growing into megacities, but the future of the countryside is less clear.」
排除：A：本地居民困境非城市未来对比重点；B：乡村会变化，但未说像城市；C：变化不可避免是演变，不是预测难易
q5.stemCn: 与城市相比，作者如何看待乡村的未来？
optionsCn: 对当地人来说将变得更加艰难。
它将类似于城市的未来。
它不太可能保持静止不变。
它比城市更难预见。

items.cn:
随着人口增长和全球城市化进程的加速，人们将大量注意力集中在城市的可持续性上，而乡村却鲜少受到关注。
乡村生活通常与紧密的社区、归属感以及简单宁静的生活方式联系在一起。然而，尽管乡村中确实存在部分或全部这些元素，但同时也存在着保守主义和就业机会匮乏的问题。乡村社区所遭受的痛苦主要归因于后者。受城市经济条件改善的吸引，世界各地的农村居民纷纷外迁，这不仅加剧了高密度城市的过度拥挤，也使乡村陷入荒凉。
那么，在这些变化中乡村如何确保其生存？或者它究竟是否应该继续存在？由于居住地与设施之间的距离较远且公共交通往往不连续，生活在乡村的人对汽车的依赖程度更高。此外，乡村居民在维护多为独立式住宅的建筑上也消耗更多能源。虽然我们在城市中可能像箱子一样被堆叠起来，但这带来了乡村无法比拟的能源效率。乡村的能源需求导致人均碳排放量高于城市，因此提倡这种生活方式实际上是不负责任的。
保护乡村是一个热门话题。那些在城市致富的人常常在乡村购买第二居所，偶尔前往体验所谓简朴的生活。这种做法的副作用是，由于需求增加推高了房价，使得当地人买不起房。目前尚未找到解决这一挑战的办法，因为市场力量正进一步迫使居民离开乡村。对于坚信乡村保存价值的人来说，这令人深感遗憾。
尽管人们对乡村持有理想化的看法很常见，但现实是乡村生活一直在不断演变。工业化带来了劳动分工的增加，改变了乡村人与人之间的社会联系。互联网将曾经陌生的文化引入了乡村。旅行交通条件的改善和可负担性的提高使世界变得更加易于接触，创造了一个“地球村”。考虑到这些变化，乡村的不断演进显然是不可避免的。
也许乡村也应该为未来大规模的人口增长做好准备。随着世界各地城市的迅速扩张，当前的城市一代人将如何应对大规模城市化带来的必然社会变革？对更简单生活的向往是否会愈发强烈，从而引发一场乡村复兴？
随着世界继续走向城市化，呼吁保护乡村的声音可能会日益高涨。但变化是不可避免的。我们知道，世界将见证新城市从尘埃中崛起，现有城市成长为巨型都市，但乡村的未来却更加模糊不清。

items.title: 2024年12月 六级真题第2套 · 第2篇
items.text:
Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned. They've become so embedded in our consciousness that people think it's absurd to think otherwise. It might be useful, however, to at least push back on this assumption because people evaluate environment, situations, and people aesthetically. We may find that we still believe it is correct, but we may also find that there is a lot more to the situation than you suppose.
A recent study exploring aesthetic taste was published in Cognition. The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.
The study found that shared taste was most common for faces and natural landscapes, but least common among works of architecture and art. The hypothesis is the commonly pleasing features, like proportion or symmetry, are at work.
Preferences for natural scenes might be learned through life experiences. Factors like habitability, safety, and openness might be preferred as people develop. Some of the details of landscapes change, but the basics are more common, e.g., water, open spaces, and signs of care.
Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.
It's possible that the lower amount of agreement in the shared taste of artifacts has to do more with elements of style, rather than "behavioral consequences".
All of the consequences seem reasonable (or at least possible), but I think there might be an interesting philosophical conclusion that they did not draw. It seems that there is an objective ground to our aesthetic preferences or evaluations. I am not saying this would mean beauty is completely objective, just that there could possibly be general objective principles at work, i.e., beauty is not simply in the eye of the beholder.
Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world. It's not exactly the same everywhere, but it is common. For example, a sunset is similar enough in different places to warrant almost universal appeal.
Possible universal principles of beauty—such as proportion, fittingness, radiance, and others—are general categories, which allow for a wide array of embodiments. When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.
This is why it's important to experience diverse cultures and their artifacts because it opens us up to different ways of approaching or constructing beauty. And it is always good to question our assumptions.

q5.stem: What does the passage say about the statement "beauty is in the eye of the beholder"?
options: It has hardly ever been disputed.
It can be interpreted aesthetically.
Many people have found it absurd.
People have long been misled by it.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Statements, like "beauty is in the eye of the beholder(观看者)", are rarely questioned.」
排除：B：原文未称该说法可审美解读；C：荒谬指相反想法而非原说法；D：原文未提及该说法误导
q5.stemCn: 文章中关于“情人眼里出西施”这句话说了什么？
optionsCn: 这句话几乎没有受到过质疑。
它可以从美学角度进行解读。
许多人发现它是荒谬的。
人们长期以来被这句话误导。

q5.stem: What does a recent study exploring aesthetic taste show?
options: Aesthetic tastes tend to differ from person to person.
Natural beauty is rarely surpassed by artificial beauty.
There is less consensus on objects shaped by human craft.
There is general agreement on what is pleasing to the eye.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The results from this study show that people agree very much in their aesthetic evaluation of natural objects, but they disagree more about artifacts, or human-made objects.」
排除：A：原文说自然对象评价高度一致，不指审美全主观；B：原文谈自然偏好因素，未称人造物共识强；D：原文指建筑艺术共识少，未说有普遍标准
q5.stemCn: 一项探索审美趣味的最新研究显示了什么？
optionsCn: 审美趣味往往因人而异。
自然美很少被人工美超越。
对于由人类工艺塑造的物体，共识较少。
对于什么是悦目的事物，存在普遍共识。

q5.stem: Why do people differ in their aesthetic appraisal of artifacts?
options: They come out in a great variety of designs.
They lead to varying behavioral consequences.
They take up much less natural space than landscapes.
They come into people's view less often than natural spaces.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Art and architecture, unlike natural spaces, do not have the same level of exposure. So, people do not have the same level of shared taste.」
排除：A：原文未将“设计种类繁多”解释为人工物审美评价分歧的原因；B：原文称低一致性可能更与风格有关，而非行为后果；C：原文比较的是曝光程度，未说人工物占用自然空间更少
q5.stemCn: 为什么人们对工艺品的美学评价各不相同？
optionsCn: 它们呈现出多种多样的设计。
它们导致不同的行为后果。
它们占用的自然空间远少于景观。
它们进入人们视野的频率低于自然景观。

q5.stem: What does the example of sunset tell about nature?
options: It creates a powerful appeal through its brilliant radiance.
It displays aesthetic traits in a similar way the world over.
It embodies beauty with a wide array of aesthetic features.
It establishes the principles of beauty in a number of ways.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Nature exhibits some of the universal aesthetic features, such as radiance, in a common way throughout the world.」
排除：A：未强调自然审美共通；C：艺术建筑共识低；D：风格分歧非日落直接说明。
q5.stemCn: 日落的例子说明了自然的什么特点？
optionsCn: 它通过其璀璨的光芒产生强烈的吸引力。
它在世界各地以相似的方式展示美学特征。
它体现了具有广泛美学特征的多种美。
它以多种方式确立了美的原则。

q5.stem: Why do artifacts not always hold universal appeal?
options: The appreciation of their beauty is not subject to objective standards.
The universal principle of beauty prevents a wide array of embodiments.
The way their creators apply the principle of beauty may not be pleasing to everybody.
Their creators interpret the universal principle of beauty each in their preferred way.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「When people get involved in making artifacts in architecture or art, they apply these very general concepts in unique ways. But the way they applied the principle may not have universal appeal.」
排除：A：原文承认客观审美原则；B：原则不会阻止多样体现；D：独特应用不等于按偏好
q5.stemCn: 为什么工艺品并不总是具有普遍的吸引力？
optionsCn: 对其美的欣赏不受客观标准的约束。
美的普遍原则阻碍了多种表现形式。
其创造者应用美的原则的方式可能不能让每个人都满意。
其创造者各自按照自己偏好的方式诠释美的普遍原则。

items.cn:
诸如“情人眼里出西施”之类的陈述很少受到质疑。它们已深深植根于我们的意识之中，以至于人们认为任何其他想法都是荒谬的。然而，至少对这个假设提出一些反思可能是有用的，因为人们在审美上评价环境、情境和人。我们可能会发现我们仍然相信它是正确的，但也可能会发现情况比我们所想象的复杂得多。
最近一项探索审美品味的研究发表在《认知》（Cognition）期刊上。该研究的结果显示，人们在自然物体的审美评估上高度一致，但在人造物品（artifacts）上的分歧更大。
研究发现，对于面孔和自然景观，共同的品味最为普遍；而对于建筑和艺术作品，共同品味则最少见。假说认为，那些普遍令人愉悦的特征，如比例或对称性，正在发挥作用。
对自然景观的偏好可能是通过生活经验习得的。随着人的成长，宜居性、安全性和开阔度等因素可能会更受青睐。景观的一些细节会发生变化，但基本要素更为常见，例如水源、开放空间以及体现关怀的迹象。
与自然空间不同，艺术和建筑并没有同等程度的曝光率。因此，人们在共享品味方面没有同等的一致性。
人造物品在共享品味上一致性较低，这可能更多地与风格元素有关，而非“行为后果”。
所有可能的解释似乎都合理（或至少有可能），但我认为他们未得出一个有趣的哲学结论。我们的审美偏好或评价似乎具有客观基础。我并非意味着美是完全客观的，只是说可能存在某些普遍的客观原则在起作用，即美不仅仅取决于观看者的眼光。
自然界在全球范围内以普遍的方式展现了一些通用的美学特征，例如光辉。它在各处并不完全相同，但是共通的。例如，不同地方的日落足够相似，从而几乎能引起普世的共鸣。
美的潜在普遍原则——如比例、适宜性、光辉等——属于广义范畴，允许有各种各样的具体表现形式。当人们参与制作建筑或艺术领域的人造物品时，他们以独特的方式应用这些非常通用的概念。但他们应用这些原则的方式未必具有普遍的吸引力。
这就是为什么体验多元文化及其人造物品如此重要，因为它让我们接触到接近或构建美的不同方式。并且，质疑我们的既定假设总是有益的。

items.src: 2024年12月 六级真题第3套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2024年12月 六级真题第3套 · 第1篇
items.text:
There are hundreds of personality quizzes online that assert they can ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant. Left-brained people are supposedly logical and excel at language and math while right-brained people are more imaginative, emotionally intelligent and skilled with spatial reasoning. There's just one problem: That's not how brains work.
Popular science enthusiasts sort of took this idea and ran with it, and it's become woven in popular culture now, and it's not going away.
Despite this enduring belief, there's no such thing as being "right-brained" or "left-brained". Whether you're someone who tends more towards creativity or logic has nothing to do with one hemisphere of your brain being dominant over the other. But the actual science of how the two halves of our brains work together is sometimes stranger than fiction.
The human brain is divided into two hemispheres, the left and right. In all vertebrate(脊椎的) animals, the right hemisphere controls the left side of the body and vice versa. And scientists have long known, thanks to the behaviors of patients who suffered brain injuries, that different areas of the brain do different things.
But many scientists struggled with this idea, because the very suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain operate differently disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry.
Work by neuroscientists(神经科学家) has revealed the importance of different hemispheres of the brain for different activities. However, their research quickly saw some misinterpretations in the general public: Some presumed creative people must be right-brained and logical people left-brained. It is proven that not only is personality unrelated to the different halves of the brain, but people aren't really right- or left-brained to begin with. The idea that we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality, is categorically false. That's never been supported in the neuroscience community. Neuroscientists don't believe that and never have.
What scientists learned is that there are really important differences between the left hemisphere and the right hemisphere. It's just that they have nothing to do with personality or whether cognitive strategy is more logical or free spirited or creative. While researchers have shown the limitations of how the hemispheres of our brains influence our lives, it's not difficult to understand the appeal of such ideas. People are endlessly fascinated by themselves and their friends, and the subtle differences in how people think about the world are really meaningful to them. When you come up with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves, we're drawn to that. It's irresistible. But you have to take it with an enormous grain of salt.

q5.stem: What do numerous personality quizzes online claim they are able to do?
options: Distinguish between the two hemispheres of one's brain.
Determine whether one is left-brained or right-brained.
