Tell if one is more of a linguist or of a mathematician.
Ascertain how one's brain performs different tasks.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「There are hundreds of personality quizzes online that assert they can ascertain whether the right or left half of your brain is dominant.」
排除：A：测验声称判断半球主导，并非区分左右半球本身；C：语言数学只是被归因于左脑，测验未以此设问；D：测验宣称判断左/右脑，未分析具体脑任务表现。
q5.stemCn: 网上大量的性格测试声称能够做什么？
optionsCn: 区分人脑的两个半球。
判断一个人是左脑主导还是右脑主导。
分辨一个人更像语言学家还是数学家。
查明大脑如何执行不同的任务。

q5.stem: What does the author say is sometimes stranger than fiction?
options: How one hemisphere of the brain impacts creativity.
How the two halves of our brains work alternately.
How the two hemispheres of our brains cooperate.
How one half of the brain dominates the other.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「But the actual science of how the two halves of our brains work together is sometimes stranger than fiction.」
排除：A：作者否定半脑与创造力有关，排除。；B：原文强调两半协同，非交替工作。；D：文中明确否认左右半脑主导。
q5.stemCn: 作者说有时比小说更离奇的是什么？
optionsCn: 大脑的一个半球如何影响创造力。
我们大脑的两半如何交替工作。
我们大脑的两个半球如何合作。
大脑的一半如何支配另一半。

q5.stem: Why did many scientists have difficulty endorsing the idea that different areas of the brain do different things?
options: It contradicts the assumption that the two hemispheres of the brain are symmetrical.
It dismisses the view that the universe has been evolving in a consistent manner.
It is in conflict with the suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain work together.
It disrupts the idea that the right hemisphere of the brain controls the left side of the body.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「But many scientists struggled with this idea, because the very suggestion that the left and right halves of the brain operate differently disrupted the idea that nature tends toward perfect symmetry.」
排除：B：原文未谈宇宙演化一致，属无关偷换；C：原文说左右确有差异，并非强调协同；D：右半球控左身只是事实，非争议原因
q5.stemCn: 为什么许多科学家难以认同大脑不同区域负责不同功能这一观点？
optionsCn: 它与大脑两个半球对称的假设相矛盾。
它否定了宇宙以一致方式演变的观点。
它与左右大脑半球协同工作的建议相冲突。
它扰乱了右脑控制身体左侧这一观念。

q5.stem: What belief have neuroscientists long rejected according to the passage?
options: There are left-dominant people and right-dominant people with different personalities.
There are noticeable differences between the left and right hemispheres of the brain.
One's personality is hardly related to the different halves of the brain.
Different areas of the brain are responsible for different activities.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「The idea that we have left-dominant people and right-dominant people, and that this is related to personality, is categorically false. That's never been supported in the neuroscience community。」
排除：B：半球确有分工差异，但非主导人格依据。；C：在线测验有吸引力，但不构成科学依据。；D：脑区功能不同，不等于左右半球主导性格。
q5.stemCn: 根据文章，神经科学家长期以来一直拒绝接受哪种信念？
optionsCn: 存在具有不同人格特征的左脑主导者和右脑主导者。
大脑左右半球之间存在显著差异。
个人的人格与大脑的不同半球几乎无关。
大脑的不同区域负责不同的活动。

q5.stem: What are we advised to do with an online quiz that tells us something about ourselves?
options: Challenge its authority.
Scrutinize its originality.
Evaluate its popularity.
Question its reliability.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「It's irresistible. But you have to take it with an enormous grain of salt.」
排除：A：原文未提挑战其权威，只说别轻信测验结果。；B：原文未要求审视测验的原创性，只谈其可信度。；C：原文未让评估测验流行度，而是提醒别太当真。
q5.stemCn: 对于告诉我们关于自身某些信息的在线测试，我们被建议怎么做？
optionsCn: 挑战其权威性。
审查其原创性。
评估其流行度。
质疑其可靠性。

items.cn:
网上有数百种性格测试声称能够确定你的左脑还是右脑占主导地位。据说左脑主导的人逻辑思维强，擅长语言和数学；而右脑主导的人更具想象力、情感智力更高且空间推理能力更强。然而有一个问题：大脑并非如此运作。
科普爱好者们在某种程度上接受了这一观点并广为传播，如今它已融入流行文化，且并未消退。
尽管这种信念经久不衰，但并不存在所谓的“右脑型”或“左脑型”人格。一个人更倾向于创造力还是逻辑性，与其大脑某一半球支配另一半球毫无关系。但实际上，我们大脑两半球协同工作的科学原理有时比小说还要离奇。
人类大脑分为左右两个半球。在所有脊椎动物中，右半球控制身体左侧，反之亦然。科学家早已知道（得益于对脑损伤患者行为的研究），大脑的不同区域负责不同的功能。
但许多科学家曾难以接受这一观念，因为暗示左右半球运作方式不同，违背了自然界趋向完美对称的理念。
神经科学研究揭示了大脑不同半球对不同活动的重要性。然而，公众对其研究结果迅速产生了误解：一些人认为富有创造力的人必是右脑主导，逻辑性强的人必是左脑主导。事实证明，不仅个性与大脑半球无关，而且人根本不存在所谓的右脑或左脑主导类型。“我们有左脑主导者和右脑主导者，且这与个性相关”的观点纯属谬误。这一点从未得到神经科学界的支持，神经学家也不相信这种说法，过去也从未相信过。
科学家认识到，左右半球之间确实存在重要差异，只是这些差异与个性或认知策略偏向逻辑、自由奔放还是创造性毫无关联。尽管研究者已表明大脑半球如何影响我们的生活有其局限性，但这种理念的吸引力并不难理解。人们对自己和朋友充满无尽的好奇，人们思考世界的细微差异对他们而言意义重大。当你遇到一个能告诉你关于自身信息的在线测试时，你就会被吸引。这令人无法抗拒。但你必须对其持极大的怀疑态度。

items.src: 2024年12月 六级真题第3套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2024年12月 六级真题第3套 · 第2篇
items.text:
One hundred thirty-five students, four teachers, one giant classroom: This is what 9th grade looks like at Westwood High School, in Mesa, Arizona's largest school system. There, an innovative teaching model has taken hold, and is spreading to other schools in the district and beyond.
Five years ago, faced with high teacher turnover and declining student enrollment, Westwood's leaders decided to try something different. Working with professors at Arizona State University's teachers college, they piloted a classroom model known as team teaching, which allows teachers to dissolve the walls that separate their classes across physical or grade divides.
The teachers share large groups of students—sometimes 100 or more—and rotate between group instruction, one-on-one interventions, small study groups, or whatever the teachers as a team agree is a priority that day. What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan: Each morning, the Westwood teams meet to hammer out a personalized program for every student the team will focus on that day.
By giving teachers more opportunity to collaborate, Mesa's administrators hoped to fill staffing gaps and boost teacher morale and retention. Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off.
"Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it's very rare a teacher walks into another room to see what's happening," said Andi Fourlis, superintendent of Mesa Public Schools. "Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation."
Of course, overhauling teaching approaches can't fix all the frustrations teachers have, such as low pay, but early results from Mesa show team teaching may be helping to reverse low morale. In a survey of hundreds of the district's teachers, researchers found those who worked on teams reported greater job satisfaction, more frequent collaborations with colleagues, and more positive interactions with students.
Another benefit of teams, teachers say, is that they can help each other improve their instruction. During one planning session, English teacher Jeff Hall shared a performance appraisal with a science teacher: Her recent lecture on something she called "the central dogma of biology" had bewildered him and their other teammates.
"If the science is too confusing for me, can you imagine the frustration you feel as kids?" Hall said. But the science teacher, he said, wouldn't have known about the confusion on her own.
The model is not for everyone. Some teachers approached about volunteering for a team have said they prefer to work alone. Team teaching can also be a scheduling nightmare, especially at schools like Westwood where only some staff work in teams. There are also thorny questions like how to evaluate four teachers on the performance of 135 students. But for the time being, it seems to be working.

q5.stem: What do we learn about team teaching from the passage?
options: It is generally conducted in classrooms without walls.
It allows students to choose teachers they favor most.
It prioritizes peer work over classroom instruction.
It is closely coordinated despite seeming confusion.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「What looks at times like chaos is in fact a carefully orchestrated plan: Each morning, the Westwood teams meet to hammer out a personalized program for every student the team will focus on that day.」
排除：A：并非无墙教室，而是跨班协作；B：未提学生自选喜欢老师；C：未提同伴优先于课堂。
q5.stemCn: 从文章中我们了解到关于团队教学的什么信息？
optionsCn: 它通常在没有墙壁的教室里进行。
它允许学生选择他们最喜欢的老师。
它优先考虑同伴作业而非课堂教学。
尽管看似混乱，但它协调紧密。

q5.stem: What does initial research suggest regarding Westwood's innovative teaching model?
options: It could help raise teachers' pay.
It could turn out to be a success.
It could cut down overall costs.
It could end up like a gamble.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Initial research suggests the gamble could pay off.」
排除：A：原文未提涨薪，且说低薪问题难解。；C：未提节约成本，只说研究可能奏效。；D：日程麻烦是模型缺点，非研究结论。
q5.stemCn: 初步研究表明韦斯特伍德的创新教学模式有什么结果？
optionsCn: 它可能有助于提高教师薪酬。
它可能会取得成功。
它可能削减整体成本。
它最终可能变成一场赌博。

q5.stem: What did superintendent Andi Fourlis say about the teaching profession?
options: Morale cannot be boosted until teaching models are overhauled.
Teachers are simply too busy to visit classes of their colleagues.
Progress is slow due to lack of collaboration among teachers.
Teachers often do fantastic things without being noticed.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Teachers are doing fantastic things, but it's very rare a teacher walks into another room to see what's happening," said Andi Fourlis, superintendent of Mesa Public Schools. "Our profession is so slow to advance because we are working in isolation」
排除：A：无中生有，未提教学模型改革；B：张冠李戴，是罕见参观而非太忙；D：与原文相反。
q5.stemCn: 督学安迪·富利斯对教学工作说了什么？
optionsCn: 除非彻底改革教学模式，否则无法提振士气。
老师们太忙了，以至于没时间去同事的课堂观摩。
由于缺乏教师间的合作，进展缓慢。
老师们经常做出出色的事情而不被注意到。

q5.stem: What does the author want to show by citing English teacher Jeff Hall's experience?
options: English teachers and science teachers are complementary in performing their tasks.
A teacher of arts and letters is completely puzzled by what a science teacher teaches.
The new teaching model helps inform the teacher how their instruction is received.
Science teachers will hardly know the confusion they create without a performance appraisal.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「But the science teacher, he said, wouldn't have known about the confusion on her own.」
排除：A：例子非任务互补，是团队反馈；B：非完全困惑，重点在获知反应；D：无考核未必绝对不知，过度推断
q5.stemCn: 作者引用英语老师杰夫·霍尔的经历想说明什么？
optionsCn: 英语老师和科学老师在完成任务时是互补的。
文科老师完全对科学老师教的内容感到困惑。
新的教学模式帮助老师了解他们的教学是如何被接受的。
如果没有绩效评估，科学老师很难知道他们造成的困惑。

q5.stem: What does the author think is one of the difficult problems in implementing the new teaching model?
options: What to do with teachers working alone.
What to include in teaching schedules.
How to recruit volunteers for a team.
How to assess each teacher's performance.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「There are also thorny questions like how to evaluate four teachers on the performance of 135 students.」
排除：A：教师偏好单干，未述如何处置；B：日程难为排班，非内容安排；C：招募志愿者非实施难点。
q5.stemCn: 作者认为实施新教学模式的一个难点是什么？
optionsCn: 如何处理单独工作的教师。
教学日程表中应包含哪些内容。
如何招募团队成员志愿者。
如何评估每位教师的绩效。

items.cn:
一百三十五名学生，四位教师，一间巨大的教室：这就是亚利桑那州最大学区梅萨市韦斯特伍德高中九年级的样子。在那里，一种创新的教学模式已经扎根，并正在向该学区及其他地区的学校推广。
五年前，面对高教师流动率和学生入学率下降的问题，韦斯特伍德的领导者决定尝试新举措。他们与亚利桑那州立大学教育学院的合作，试点了一种名为“团队教学”的课堂模式，允许教师打破物理空间或年级划分造成的班级隔阂。
教师们共同管理大型学生群体——有时超过100人——并在集体授课、一对一干预、小组学习或其他团队协商确定的当日优先事项之间轮换。表面看起来有时像混乱的场景，实际上却是精心编排的计划：每天早晨，韦斯特伍德的教师团队会面，为当天重点关注每个学生制定个性化方案。
通过给予教师更多协作机会，梅萨的教育管理者希望填补人员空缺，提升教师士气和留任率。初步研究表明，这一赌注可能带来回报。
梅萨公立学校总监安迪·福利斯表示：“老师们在做很棒的工作，但很少有老师走进另一个教室看看里面发生了什么。由于我们在孤立状态下工作，我们的职业发展非常缓慢。”
当然，彻底改革教学方法无法解决教师面临的所有挫折感，比如低薪问题，但梅萨的早期结果显示，团队教学可能有助于扭转低迷的士气。在对该地区数百名教师的调查中，研究人员发现，参与团队工作的教师报告了更高的工作满意度、更频繁的同事协作以及与学生更积极的互动。
教师们说，团队的另一个好处是可以帮助彼此改进教学。在一次备课环节中，英语教师杰夫·霍尔与一位科学教师分享了一份绩效评估：她最近关于所谓“生物学中心法则”的讲座让他和其他团队成员感到困惑。
霍尔说：“如果科学内容连我都觉得太令人困惑，想象一下孩子们的感受吧。”但他指出，如果没有外界反馈，这位科学教师自己永远不会意识到学生的困惑。
这种模式并不适合所有人。有些被邀请自愿加入团队教学的教师表示更喜欢单独工作。团队教学也会带来排课难题，尤其是在像韦斯特伍德这样只有部分员工采用团队模式的学校，协调起来简直是噩梦。此外，如何根据135名学生的表现来评估4位教师的绩效也是一个棘手问题。但就目前而言，这一模式似乎行之有效。

items.src: 2025年6月 六级真题第1套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2025年6月 六级真题第1套 · 第1篇
items.text:
Nationally, one in six children miss 15 or more days of school in a year. Education officials have deplored all this missed instruction.
These chronically absent students suffer academically because of all the classroom instruction they miss out on. In 2015, the U.S. secretary of education responded to this crisis, urging communities to support every student to attend every day and be successful in school. His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.
Worrying about whether children attend school makes sense. After all, if students don't show up, teachers can't teach them.
But what if America's attendance crisis is about much more than students missing class? What if, instead, it is a reflection of family and community crises these students face—such as being ejected from the family apartment, fearing for their safety in their neighborhood or suffering an illness?
As social scientists we investigated how excused and unexcused absences relate to children's academic achievement.
We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning. In fact, children with no unexcused absences—but 15 to 18 excused absences—have test scores equal to their peers who have no absences.
Meanwhile, the average child with even just one unexcused absence does much worse academically than peers with none.
We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children's academic progress.
Our evidence suggests unexcused absences are problematic, but for a different reason than people often think. Absence from school, and especially unexcused absence, matters mainly as a signal of many crises children and their families may be facing. It matters less as a cause of lower student achievement due to missed instruction.
How we choose to think of school absences matters for educational policy. School attendance policies typically hold schools and families accountable for the days children miss, regardless of whether they were excused or unexcused absences.
These policies assume that missing school for any reason harms children academically because they are missing classroom instruction. They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences. We find neither to be the case.
As a result, these attendance policies end up disproportionately punishing families dealing with out-of-school crises in their lives and pressuring schools who serve them to get students to school more often.
We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.

q5.stem: What does the U.S. secretary of education say in his open letter?
options: It is of vital importance to respond promptly to the school absence crisis.
The academic performance of chronically absent students is deplorable.
Low academic achievement is mainly attributed to school absences.
The effect of school absences on American education is worrisome.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「His open letter stated that missing 10% of school days in a year for any reason—excused or unexcused—is a primary cause of low academic achievement.」
排除：A：原文未提紧迫应对，只说回应危机并呼吁支持；B：原文信中指缺勤是低成绩原因，未泛谈学业表现；C：正确，信中指出缺勤是低学业成就主要原因。
q5.stemCn: 美国教育部长在他的公开信中说了什么？
optionsCn: 迅速应对学生缺勤危机至关重要。
长期缺勤学生的学业表现令人遗憾。
低学业成就主要归因于学校缺勤。
学校缺勤对美国教育的影响令人担忧。

q5.stem: What do the authors find about school absences?
options: Excused school absences have little impact on children's learning.
There is little difference between unexcused and excused absences.
Excused absences lead to comparatively better school performance.
Unexcused absences are a big challenge to both schools and families.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「We find that absences excused by a parent do little to harm children's learning.」
排除：B：原文指出无故缺勤成绩更差，二者影响并不小；C：原文只说请假缺勤影响小，未说其比无缺勤更好；D：文章称无故缺勤是家庭困境信号，非学校挑战。
q5.stemCn: 关于学校缺勤，作者发现了什么？
optionsCn: 有理由的缺勤对儿童学习影响很小。
无正当理由缺勤和有理由缺勤之间几乎没有区别。
有理由的缺勤导致相对较好的学校表现。
无正当理由缺勤对学校和家庭都是巨大挑战。

q5.stem: What do the authors believe concerning unexcused school absences?
options: They are likely to cause a decrease in students' academic achievements due to missed instruction.
They point directly to many of the out-of-school challenges confronting children and their families.
They are matters the American government typically ignores when formulating educational policies.
They give a clear signal to children and their families of the crises they are likely to face in the future.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「We believe unexcused absence is a strong signal of the many challenges children and families face, including economic and medical hardships. Unexcused absences can be a powerful signal of how those out-of-school challenges affect children's academic progress.」
排除：A：家长准假几乎不影响学习，排除缺课致成绩下降；C：出勤政策并非忽视问题，而是问责方式不当；D：缺勤是已有家庭挑战的信号，非造成新挑战。
q5.stemCn: 关于无正当理由的学校缺勤，作者的观点是什么？
optionsCn: 由于错过教学，它们可能导致学生学业成绩下降。
它们直接指向儿童及其家庭面临的许多校外挑战。
它们是美国政府制定教育政策时通常忽视的问题。
它们向儿童及其家庭发出了他们未来可能面临危机的明确信号。

q5.stem: What is the assumption underlying education policies in the U.S.?
options: Children's academic performance depends on reducing the number of absences.
Schools can boost children's academic performance by effective intervention.
Schools as well as families should be held responsible for out-of-school crises.
Children's academic performance is closely related to the quality of instruction.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「They also assume that schools will be able to effectively intervene by reducing student absences.」
排除：A：原文否认减少缺勤能提升成绩，缺勤只是危机信号；C：政策问责缺勤日，并非要求家庭为校外危机担责；D：政策假设缺课损失教学，而非强调教学质量高低。
q5.stemCn: 美国教育政策背后的假设是什么？
optionsCn: 儿童的学业表现取决于减少缺勤次数。
学校可以通过有效的干预措施提高儿童的学业表现。
学校和家庭都应对校外危机负责。
儿童的学业表现与教学质量密切相关。

q5.stem: What do the authors suggest doing regarding school absences?
options: Identifying their underlying causes.
Reframing school attendance policies.
Directing resources to helping needy children.
Pressuring schools to reduce unexcused ones.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「We instead suggest using unexcused absence from school as a signal to channel resources to the children and families who need them most.」
排除：A：原文建议将缺勤视为需要资源的信号，并非单纯减少缺勤；B：作者指出不能只追究学校，而应以缺勤信号配置资源；D：文章虽谈家庭困难，但主张据此帮扶而非只识别原因。
q5.stemCn: 关于学校缺勤问题，作者建议怎么做？
optionsCn: 找出其根本原因。
重新制定学校出勤政策。
将资源用于帮助贫困儿童。
施压学校减少无正当理由的缺勤。

items.cn:
在全国范围内，每六个儿童中就有一个每年缺课15天或更多。教育官员对这种缺失的教学表示痛惜。
这些长期缺课的学生因为错过了大量的课堂指导而在学业上遭受损失。2015年，美国教育部长回应了这一危机，敦促社区支持每一位学生每天到校并在学校取得成功。他的公开信指出，无论出于何种原因——无论是请假还是无故缺席——一年中缺课达到10%是学业成绩低下的主要原因。
担心孩子是否上学是有道理的。毕竟，如果学生不露面，老师就无法教导他们。
但是，如果美国的出勤率危机不仅仅是学生缺课的问题呢？相反，它是否反映了这些学生所面临的家庭和社区危机——例如被逐出家庭公寓、在社区中感到安全受威胁或患病？
作为社会科学家，我们调查了请假和无故缺勤与儿童学业成就之间的关系。
我们发现，由家长批准的缺勤对儿童学习造成的损害微乎其微。事实上，没有无故缺勤但有15到18次请假缺勤的儿童，其测试成绩与零缺勤的同龄人相当。
与此同时，即使只有一次无故缺勤的平均儿童，其学业表现也远不如零缺勤的同龄人。
我们认为，无故缺勤是儿童和家庭面临的诸多挑战（包括经济和医疗困难）的一个强烈信号。无故缺勤可以有力地表明校外的这些挑战如何影响儿童的学业进步。
我们的证据表明，无故缺勤是个问题，但原因与人们通常认为的不同。缺勤，尤其是无故缺勤，主要作为一个信号，表明儿童及其家庭可能正面临许多危机。相比之下，将其视为因错过教学而导致学生成绩下降的原因则没那么重要。
我们如何看待缺勤问题对教育政策至关重要。学校的出勤政策通常要求学校和家庭对儿童缺勤的天数负责，无论这些缺勤是请假还是无故缺席。
这些政策假设，无论出于什么原因缺课，都会因学生错过课堂教学而损害他们的学业。它们还假设学校能够通过减少学生缺勤来进行有效干预。我们发现这两点都不成立。
结果，这些出勤政策最终不成比例地惩罚了那些在生活中面临校外危机的家庭，并给服务于这些家庭的学校施加压力，迫使它们更频繁地将学生送到学校。
相反，我们建议将学校的无故缺勤作为一个信号，以便将资源引导给最需要它们的儿童和家庭。

items.src: 2025年6月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2025年6月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.text:
After earning a bachelor's degree, I was determined to do what I love. I headed straight to graduate school to investigate the social problems that fascinated me.
For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled. "You can figure out the employment stuff later."
It wasn't until I began to research this widely accepted career advice that I understood how problematic it really was.
As a sociologist, I interviewed college students and professional workers to learn what it really meant to pursue their dreams, which I will refer to here as the passion principle. I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.
Surveys show the American public has long held the passion principle in high regard as a career decision-making priority. And its popularity is even stronger among those facing job instability.
Advocates of the passion principle found it compelling because they believed that following one's passion can provide workers with both the motivation necessary to work hard and a place to find fulfillment.
Yet, what I found is that following one's passion does not necessarily lead to fulfillment, but is one of the most powerful cultural forces perpetuating overwork. I also found that promoting the pursuit of one's passion helps perpetuate social inequalities due to the fact that not everyone has the same economic resources to allow them to pursue their passion with ease.
While the passion principle is broadly popular, not everyone has the necessary resources to turn their passion into a stable, good-paying job. Passion-seekers from wealthy families are better able to wait until a job they are passionate about comes along without worrying about student loans in the meantime. They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs. Surveys revealed that working-class and first-generation college graduates, regardless of their career field, are more likely than their wealthier peers to end up in low-paying unskilled jobs when they pursue their passion.
Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.
It's not just well-off passion-seekers who benefit from the passion principle. Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay. They even sacrifice a good salary, job stability and leisure time to work in a job they love.

q5.stem: What did the author advise people do for almost a decade?
options: Figure out what is the most fascinating job.
Follow widely accepted career counsel.
Pursue their careers with passion.
Do whatever they are zealous for.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「For almost a decade, I told everyone I encountered that they should do the same. "Follow your passion," I counseled.」
排除：A：未提寻找最吸引人的工作，而是追随热情；B：他劝的是追随热情，不是泛泛遵循职业建议；C：文中说追随热情，未说带着热情追求职业
q5.stemCn: 近十年来，作者建议人们做什么？
optionsCn: 弄清楚最迷人的工作是什么。
遵循广泛接受的职业建议。
带着热情追求他们的事业。
做他们热衷的任何事情。

q5.stem: How did the author feel about the passion principle through his research?
options: He was astonished by its consequences.
He was further convinced of its soundness.
He was actually right to follow it through.
He was struck by its broad popularity.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「I was stunned by what I found out about this principle in the research for my new book.」
排除：B：非怀疑，作者震惊其发现；C：非乐观，作者强调问题；D：非冷漠，作者关注后果
q5.stemCn: 通过研究，作者对“热情原则”有何感受？
optionsCn: 他对其后果感到惊讶。
他更加确信其合理性。
他坚持这一原则实际上是正确的。
他被其广泛的流行所震撼。

q5.stem: What is important to turning one's passion into a stable, good-paying job?
options: Willingness to take unpaid internships and low-paying jobs.
Full academic preparedness and sound career counseling.
Hard work and sacrifice of leisure time.
Financial backing and social connections.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「They are also better situated to take unpaid internships to get their foot in the door while their parents pay their rent. And they often have access to parents' social networks to help them find jobs.」
排除：A：无偿实习/低薪需家庭资助，仅愿意不够；B：学术准备与职业咨询未被指为核心条件；C：努力牺牲休闲是雇主获益机制，非答案
q5.stemCn: 要将一个人的热情转化为稳定的、高薪的工作，什么很重要？
optionsCn: 愿意接受无薪实习和低薪工作。
充分的学术准备和可靠的职业咨询。
努力工作并牺牲休闲时间。
资金支持和社会关系。

q5.stem: What happens when everyone is encouraged to follow their passion?
options: Many more career aspirants end up unemployed.
People are less concerned with socioeconomic inequality.
Socioeconomic inequality is likely to persist.
Career counselors are going to lose credibility.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Colleges, workplaces and career counselors who promote the "follow your passion" path for everyone, without leveling the playing field, help perpetuate socioeconomic inequalities among career aspirants.」
排除：A：文中未提更多人失业，只说低薪无技能岗位。；B：未称人们不关心不平等，反建议资源帮扶。；D：未指咨询师失去信誉，只述其助长不平等。
q5.stemCn: 当每个人都受到鼓励去追随自己的热情时会发生什么？
optionsCn: 更多的求职者最终失业。
人们对社会经济不平等的关注度降低。
社会经济不平等可能会持续存在。
职业顾问将失去信誉。

q5.stem: What does the author say about employers of passionate workers?
options: They provide these workers with job stability and a good salary.
They exploit these workers' passion to benefit themselves.
They level the playing field for these workers to reach their goals.
They encourage these workers to realize their aspirations.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Employers of passionate workers do, too. Potential employers showed greater interest in passionate applicants in part because they believed the applicants would work hard at their jobs without expecting an increase in pay.」
排除：A：原文说雇主也受益，未称其保障薪资与稳定。；C：原文称雇主持续受益并压榨，未说其反对该原则。；D：原文说雇主感兴趣因员工苦干少加薪，非关注公平。
q5.stemCn: 关于雇佣充满热情的员工，作者说了什么？
optionsCn: 他们为这些员工提供工作稳定性和良好的薪水。
他们利用这些员工的热情来为自己谋利。
他们为这些员工创造公平的竞争环境以实现目标。
他们鼓励这些员工实现他们的抱负。

items.cn:
在获得学士学位后，我决心做自己喜欢的事。我径直去读研究生，研究令我着迷的社会问题。
在近十年的时间里，我告诉每一个遇到的人应该效仿我。“追随你的激情，”我建议道，“你可以以后再解决就业问题。”
直到我开始研究这一被广泛接受的职业建议时，我才明白它实际上存在多大的问题。
作为一名社会学家，我采访了大学生和专业人士，以了解追求梦想的真正含义，我在这里称之为“激情原则”。在为我的新书进行研究时，我对这一原则的发现感到震惊。
调查显示，长期以来，美国公众一直高度重视激情原则，将其作为职业决策的优先事项。而在面临工作不稳定的人群中，这一原则的流行程度甚至更高。
激情原则的支持者发现它具有吸引力，因为他们相信追随一个人的激情可以为工作者提供努力工作所需的动力以及找到满足感的场所。
然而，我发现，追随个人的激情并不一定能带来满足感，而是助长过度工作的最强大的文化力量之一。我还发现，提倡追求个人激情有助于延续社会不平等，原因在于并非每个人都有相同的经济资源来轻松追求自己的激情。
虽然激情原则广受欢迎，但并非每个人都有必要的资源将激情转化为稳定且高薪的工作。来自富裕家庭的激情追求者更能等待一份他们充满热情的工作出现，而不必担心期间的学生贷款。在他们父母支付房租的同时，他们也更有条件参加无薪实习以获得入门机会。而且，他们往往能接触到父母的社会网络来帮助找工作。调查显示，无论从事哪个职业领域，工人阶级和第一代大学毕业生比家境更富裕的同龄人更有可能在追求激情后陷入低薪的非技术性工作。
大学、职场和职业顾问在不消除起跑线不平等的情况下，向所有人推广“追随你的激情”这条路，这有助于延续职业追求者之间的社会经济不平等。
受益于此激情原则的不仅仅是富有的激情追求者。雇用有激情的员工的雇主也从中受益。潜在雇主对有激情的申请人表现出更大的兴趣，部分原因是他们认为这些申请人会努力工作而不期望加薪。他们甚至愿意牺牲良好的薪水。

items.src: 2025年6月 六级真题第2套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2025年6月 六级真题第2套 · 第1篇
items.text:
Why are we so worried about our careers? Partly it's to do with money, but there's a psychological aspect to our fears as well.
We worry because we suspect—not wrongly—that the world is full of a frightening sort of person ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob.
A snob is anyone who takes a relatively small part of us and uses it to come to a rigid conclusion about how much of their attention we deserve. In the past, that might be your ancestry and royal connections. Nowadays, the snob cares about one thing only: what you do for a living.
This explains why the first question we will be asked in any new social context is 'What do you do?' and according to how we answer, snobs will either welcome us with broad smiles, or leave us in the cold.
And that is why we are fired up by such a desperate urge to achieve and impress.
Sometimes our behaviour is mistaken for greed and vanity, but it is more than this. A lot of our interest in fancy cars, jobs and houses has nothing to do with materialism. It has to do with a hunger for the respect and esteem that is only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods. It isn't the goods themselves we seek, it is the love we stand to gain through our possession of them. The next time we see someone driving a Ferrari, we shouldn't condemn them for their greed, we should pity them for the intensity of their need for love from the world.
At the root of snobbery is a lack of imagination and confidence about how to decide who in the world is valuable. The snobs are brutally misguided and slavish in their beliefs about how the superior individuals can be identified. For snobs, it is the already acclaimed and already successful who are the only ones worthy of respect. There is no room in their timid regimented minds to imagine that someone might be clever, kind or good—and yet somehow have been overlooked entirely by society, their qualities lying hidden beneath an unfamiliar veil, and having as yet discovered no obvious outlet.
The true answer to snobbery is not to say that there is no such thing as a better or worse person, but to insist that better or worse exist in constantly unexpected places and carry none of the outward signs of distinction. And because we are such poor judges of the worth of others, our ultimate duty remains to be kind, good, curious and imaginative about pretty much everyone who ever crosses our path.

q5.stem: What gives rise to our worry about careers apart from money?
options: Fear of being judged in a snobbish manner.
The prospect of facing fault-finding managers.
The ruthless way employees are often treated.
Fright at the difficulty in hunting for a job.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「We worry because we suspect—not wrongly—that the world is full of a frightening sort of person ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob.」
排除：B：原文未提找工作的困难，只是担心被势利之人评判；C：文中指势利者评判，不是员工通常被残酷对待；D：未提求职难度或害怕找工作难，属无中生有。
q5.stemCn: 除了金钱之外，还有什么引发了我们对职业的担忧？
optionsCn: 害怕被以势利的方式评判。
面临挑剔的管理者的前景。
员工经常被对待的残酷方式。
对求职困难的恐惧。

q5.stem: What do we learn from the passage about today's snobs?
options: They try hard to dig into a person's past.
They draw a rigid conclusion about people.
They judge a person by their occupation.
They tend to place people in a social context.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Nowadays, the snob cares about one thing only: what you do for a living.」
排除：A：查过去血统属旧例，非当今标准。；B：泛指刚性下结论，未点出当今标准是职业。；D：社交语境只是场景，非评判依据。
q5.stemCn: 从文章中我们了解到今天的势利眼有什么特点？
optionsCn: 他们努力挖掘一个人的过去。
他们对人做出僵化的结论。
他们通过职业来评判一个人。
他们倾向于将人置于社会背景中。

q5.stem: What does the author say about people's interest in material goods?
options: It is the cause for condemnation of their greed.
It has a lot to do with the comforts they provide.
It arouses pity rather than respect from the wealthy.
It arises from their craving for social recognition.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「A lot of our interest in fancy cars, jobs and houses has nothing to do with materialism. It has to do with a hunger for the respect and esteem that is only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods.」
排除：A：原文说不应因贪婪谴责，非导致谴责的原因；B：兴趣并非源于物质主义，而是求尊重；C：原文说不是物质本身，而是借物质获爱
q5.stemCn: 作者关于人们对物质财富的兴趣说了什么？
optionsCn: 这是谴责他们贪婪的原因。
这与它们提供的舒适程度有很大关系。
这引起富人的怜悯而非尊重。
这源于他们对社会认可的渴望。

q5.stem: What kind of people do snobs deem worth respect and esteem?
options: Those with fame and fortune.
Those with regimented minds.
Those with intelligence and imagination.
Those with qualities lying hidden in disguise.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「For snobs, it is the already acclaimed and already successful who are the only ones worthy of respect.」
排除：B：聪明善良者，snob 不认可；C：品质被掩盖者，snob 无法识别；D：文中未提该群体，与原文不符。
q5.stemCn: 势利眼认为什么样的人值得尊重和推崇？
optionsCn: 那些有名望和财富的人。
那些思维僵化的人。
那些有智慧和想象力的人。
那些品质隐藏在伪装之下的人。

q5.stem: What does the author imply we should do to avoid being snobbish?
options: Be aware there has never been such a thing as a better or worse person.
Be kind to and curious about those who we happen to meet in our lives.
Realize that better or worse keeps changing in unexpected ways.
Judge people on the basis of their distinctive character traits.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「And because we are such poor judges of the worth of others, our ultimate duty remains to be kind, good, curious and imaginative about pretty much everyone who ever crosses our path.」
排除：A：原文承认存在更优更差的人，选项相反；C：只说好坏在意外处，未点明应善意好奇待人；D：原文反对凭外在标志评判，非据此断定
q5.stemCn: 作者暗示我们应该怎么做才能避免变得势利？
optionsCn: 意识到从来就没有所谓更好或更坏的人。
对我们生活中偶遇的人保持善良和好奇。
认识到好与坏会以意想不到的方式不断变化。
根据人们独特的性格特征来评判他人。

items.cn:
我们为何如此担忧自己的职业生涯？部分原因在于金钱，但我们的恐惧背后也有心理因素。
我们之所以焦虑，是因为我们怀疑——这种怀疑并非毫无道理——世界上充斥着一种可怕的人：他们随时准备对我们进行无情且迅速的评判；我们可以称这类人为“势利小人”。
所谓势利小人，是指那些只关注我们的某一小部分特征，并据此武断地断定我们值得他们投入多少注意力的人。在过去，这或许指的是你的家世和皇室关系。而如今，势利小人只关心一件事：你的职业。
这就解释了为什么在任何新的社交场合中，我们被问到的第一个问题总是“你是做什么的？”以及根据我们的回答，势利小人要么会以灿烂的笑容欢迎我们，要么会让我们吃闭门羹。
这也是为什么我们会被那种渴望成就和自我展示的迫切冲动所驱使。
有时，我们的行为会被误解为贪婪和虚荣，但其本质远不止于此。我们对豪车、高薪工作和豪宅的浓厚兴趣与物质主义无关。它关乎的是一种对尊重和认可的渴望，而在我们的社会中，这种尊重只能通过获取物质财富来获得。我们追求的不是物品本身，而是通过拥有这些物品可能赢得的爱。下次当我们看到有人驾驶法拉利时，我们不应谴责他们的贪婪，而应怜悯他们对世界之爱的强烈需求。
势利眼的根源在于缺乏想象力和信心去判断世上谁是有价值的。势利小人在识别优秀个体的信念上是残酷的误导者和盲从者。在他们眼中，只有那些已经获得赞誉和成功的人才配受到尊重。在他们怯懦且僵化的头脑中，没有空间去想象某人可能聪明、善良或美好——却不知何故被社会完全忽视，其品质隐藏在陌生的面纱之下，尚未找到明显的出口。
应对势利眼的真正答案不是说世上没有优劣之分的人，而是要坚持认为，更优秀或更糟糕的人存在于不断出人意料的地方，且不带有外在的区别标志。正因为我们是他人价值蹩脚的评判者，我们最终的义务是对几乎所有经过我们生命的人保持友善、良善、好奇和富有想象力。

items.src: 2025年6月 六级真题第2套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2025年6月 六级真题第2套 · 第2篇
items.text:
Women have historically been paid less. But in the US in the 1980s, they began to catch up—fast. During that decade, the gender pay gap closed by about one percentage point a year. Had that trend continued, the gender wage gap would have been closed by 2017.
But the trend didn't continue, and the gap remains yawning.
According to a new study from academics at Harvard, the stagnation can be put down, perhaps counterintuitively, to the introduction of state and federal family leave policies.
The academics argue that during the 1990s, as governments began to introduce leave policies, it was mainly women who took advantage of them. Though the leave policies might have helped those women to stay in the workplace—instead of dropping out to have families—those who returned saw their wages had increased at lower rates than the men.
After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.
Those monitoring the process towards salary equity at work have long watched as progress slowed in many countries around the world. In fact, that progress began to reverse during the pandemic(大流行病).
The gender pay gap is one of the most outstanding examples of that lack of parity(平等), and still exists just about everywhere. The motherhood penalty has become a shorthand for describing why: In many places, especially rich countries, women earn the same as men until they reach their childbearing years. Women who have children begin to see their salaries slip behind their male counterparts.
Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement. But it's also because mothers are passed over for raises and promotion, and because time out of the workplace sets women back, even if that time is taken voluntarily, and supported by company or government policy.
What would have happened if leave policies hadn't been introduced? The study doesn't go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now.
It's possible, however, that the journey towards wage parity would have stalled either way. If women's gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women—who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated.

q5.stem: What do we learn about the gender pay gap in the US during the 1980s?
options: It was being slowly closed.
It was shrinking rapidly.
It started to yawn.
It remained substantial.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「But in the US in the 1980s, they began to catch up—fast。」
排除：A：不是缓慢，原文强调fast；C：扩大出现在趋势停止后，非1980；D：1980差距正快速缩小，非持续显著
q5.stemCn: 关于20世纪80年代美国的性别薪酬差距，我们了解到了什么？
optionsCn: 它正在缓慢缩小。
它正在迅速缩小。
它开始扩大（出现缺口）。
它仍然很大。

q5.stem: What happened with the introduction of state and federal family leave policies?
options: The process towards salary equity at work began to reverse.
The rate of gender wage convergence started to fall noticeably.
The trend of women returning to work after childbirth started.
The narrowing of the gender pay gap attracted more attention.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.」
排除：A：进度逆转发生于疫情期间，非休假政策引入所致；C：休假助女性留职，非催生产后返岗趋势；D：薪酬差距受关注并非政策引入直接导致
q5.stemCn: 随着州和联邦家庭休假政策的引入发生了什么？
optionsCn: 工作场所实现薪资平等的进程开始逆转。
性别工资趋同的速度开始明显下降。
女性产后重返工作的趋势开始了。
性别薪酬差距的缩小吸引了更多关注。

q5.stem: What partly accounts for the slip in women's salaries?
options: The insufficient motivation women generally have for career advancement.
The opportunities numerous women give up for pay raise and promotion.
The huge amounts of time and energy women spend taking care of the family.
The lack of policy support from government and business corporations.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement.」
排除：A：未提能力不足；B：未说缺乏升职兴趣；D：政策非主因。
q5.stemCn: 部分解释女性薪资下滑的是什么原因？
optionsCn: 女性通常缺乏职业晋升的动力。
许多女性为了加薪和升职而放弃的机会。
女性在照顾家庭上花费的大量时间和精力。
政府和商业公司缺乏政策支持。

q5.stem: What does the new study say about wage parity?
options: It would have stalled if those controllable problems had not been addressed.
It would have halted if company and government had not worked together.
It would have been achieved with the complete erasure of gender biases.
It would have been attained with the continuation of the 1980s trend.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「The study doesn't go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now.」
排除：A：原文未说停滞取决于可控问题是否解决；B：原文未说公司与政府合作能促成平价；C：消除偏见并非原文认定必然达成平价
q5.stemCn: 这项新研究关于工资平等说了什么？
optionsCn: 如果没有解决那些可控的问题，工资平等早就停滞了。
如果公司和政府没有合作，工资平等早就停止了。
只有完全消除性别偏见才能实现工资平等。
延续20世纪80年代的趋势就能实现工资平等。

q5.stem: What prevents women from achieving parity with men in the final analysis?
options: Ignoring biases against women in the workplace.
Giving birth to children and taking care of them.
Failing to mandate breaks for childbirth and care.
Lacking resources to address biological problems.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「The motherhood penalty has become a shorthand for describing why: In many places, especially rich countries, women earn the same as men until they reach their childbearing years. Women who have children begin to see their salaries slip behind their male counte」
排除：A：无中生有；C：政策只是诱因而非根本原因；D：生物问题非主因。
q5.stemCn: 从根本上说，是什么阻碍了女性实现与男性的工资平等？
optionsCn: 忽视职场中对女性的偏见。
生育子女并照顾他们。
未能强制规定产假和育儿假。
缺乏解决生理问题的资源。

items.cn:
历史上，女性的薪酬一直较低。但在20世纪80年代的美国，她们开始迅速追赶上来。在那十年间，性别工资差距每年缩小约一个百分点。如果这一趋势持续下去，到2017年，性别工资差距本应已经消除。
但这一趋势并未持续，差距依然巨大。
哈佛大学学者的一项新研究指出，这种停滞不前（可能令人直觉上感到意外）可归因于州和联邦家庭休假政策的出台。
学者们认为，在20世纪90年代，随着政府开始引入休假政策，主要是女性利用了这些政策。虽然休假政策可能帮助了那些女性留在职场——而不是为了组建家庭而退出工作——但那些回归的女性发现，她们的工资增长幅度低于男性。
事实上，在美国引入家庭休假制度后，性别工资收敛的速度降至每年仅0.03个百分点，并且此后一直保持在这一水平。
长期监测职场薪资平等进程的人士目睹了许多国家进步速度的放缓。事实上，在大流行病期间，这种进步甚至开始逆转。
性别工资差距是这种不平等现象最突出的例子之一，并且在世界各地几乎都存在。“母职惩罚”已成为描述其原因的一种简略说法：在许多地方，尤其是富裕国家，女性在达到育龄期之前收入与男性持平。一旦有孩子，女性就开始发现自己的薪资落后于男性同行。
部分原因是女性承担了更多无偿的家庭劳动，这会挤占可用于工作的时间和用于职业发展的精力。但也因为母亲们在加薪和晋升时被忽视，而且离开职场的时间会让女性处于不利地位，即使这段时间是自愿休假的，且有公司或政府政策支持。
如果没有引入休假政策会发生什么？该研究没有深入探讨这个问题，只是说如果80年代的趋势持续到现在，我们本应实现平等。
然而，无论哪种情况，迈向工资平等的旅程都可能陷入停滞。如果女性在80年代取得的进步是通过消除偏见等因素实现的，那么一旦这些较不可控的问题得到解决，仍存在一个关于女性的问题——由于母乳喂养等生物学因素，女性承担生育并在早期照顾孩子的责任，迫使她们中断工作，无论这些中断是否被强制规定。

items.src: 2025年6月 六级真题第3套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2025年6月 六级真题第3套 · 第1篇
items.text:
Simulators are most often utilized within industries such as nuclear power, aviation and surgery where failure results in disastrous consequences. To maximize the value from a simulation learning experience, participants should immediately and directly apply their learning to a specific intervention within their organization.
Most organizations aspire to deploy significant change programs, only to find them nearly impossible to implement. That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.
To achieve success, an organization must build a transformation program that will allow change to be rapidly pulled across its departments and throughout its layers. Regardless of the level of senior management commitment, unless key thought leaders at all levels embrace the change, the initiative will wither and die. To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.
Allowing participants to enter a simulated environment provides them with the opportunity to experience alternative realities which can prompt them to rethink their current beliefs.
Behavioral change is not easy for most adults. Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative. Further, under normal working conditions, managers rarely see the full effect of their employee development efforts. As such, an intervention like a simulation can provide the stimulus for change.
An effective simulation can be better than experience as a learning tool because it accelerates time, compresses space, and unlike reality, is specifically designed to maximize participant learning. Simulations provide an immersive learning experience where skills, processes and knowledge all can be highlighted in a way reality cannot. The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.
Well-designed simulations can enable individuals and groups to develop a deep level of understanding about how their decisions and intuitive responses to business stimuli affect their fellow participants and the organization as a whole. To reap the benefits, however, simulations must feel like reality. At the end of the successful simulation, participants must declare "this is us." If they don't, they will view the experience as a game, which can be difficult to apply on the job, or worse, irrelevant to everyday work tasks. To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.

q5.stem: What do we learn about successful changes in organizations?
options: They can be immediately implemented with great ease.
They are usually led by organization leaders of vision.
They call for enthusiastic support from the workforce.
They often result from simulation learning experiences.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「That is largely because successful change requires more than a vision, it requires a workforce that not only doesn't resist change, but embraces it.」
排除：A：原文称变革几乎难实施。；B：原文说成功变革不止需愿景。；D：原文仅称模拟器助变革。
q5.stemCn: 关于组织中成功的变革，我们了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它们可以非常轻松地立即实施。
它们通常由具有远见的组织领导层发起。
它们需要员工的热情支持。
它们往往源于模拟学习体验。

q5.stem: What should learning leaders do to arouse learners' passion for change?
options: Allow them to see what could possibly be achieved.
Help them break free from their old paradigms.
Encourage them to rethink their thought models.
Stimulate them to embrace fresh opportunities.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「To create this kind of widespread passion, learning leaders must expose the workforce to what could be, which will enable them to rethink their mental models, enable them to break free from their deep-rooted paradigms and embrace the opportunity to learn.」
排除：B：属暴露未来后的结果，非领导做法；C：由暴露未来促成，非首要；D：原文指学习机会，非宽泛机会。
q5.stemCn: 为了激发学习者对变革的热情，学习领导者应该做什么？
optionsCn: 让他们看到可能取得的成就。
帮助他们摆脱旧的范式。
鼓励他们重新思考他们的思维模型。
激励他们拥抱新的机遇。

q5.stem: What does the passage say about lectures, training programs and workshops?
options: They are generally incapable of changing workers' behaviors on the job.
They are interventions different from simulations in creating stimuli for change.
They aim at transforming the behaviors of the workers in an organization.
They help managers achieve the full effect of employee development efforts.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Lectures, training programs and workshops can explain the intellectual elements of transformation, but they are seldom effective at getting to the behavioral aspects that lie at the heart of a significant change initiative.」
排除：B：原文未比较二者创造变化刺激的差异；C：原文说其难以触及行为层面，非目标；D：原文称常态下经理难看到发展成效
q5.stemCn: 文章是如何描述讲座、培训项目和研讨会的？
optionsCn: 它们通常无法改变员工在工作中的行为。
它们是不同于模拟的干预措施，在创造变革刺激方面有所不同。
它们旨在转变组织内员工的行为。
它们帮助管理者实现员工发展工作的全部效果。

q5.stem: What makes simulation one of the most fruitful forms of learning?
options: Its capability of saving time by accelerating the immersive learning experience.
Its potential for learners to examine their skills, knowledge and learning process.
Its capability of providing all participants with a practical learning experience.
Its potential for learners to explore, experiment and practice without any risk.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「The ability to explore, experiment and repeatedly apply new knowledge in unlimited, risk-free models is what makes simulation one of the most productive forms of learning.」
排除：A：加速只是设计优势，非根本原因；B：展示技能只是效果，非决定因素；C：原文强调无风险，非普通实践
q5.stemCn: 是什么使模拟成为最富有成效的学习形式之一？
optionsCn: 它能够通过加速沉浸式学习体验来节省时间。
它使学习者能够审视自己的技能、知识和学习过程。
它能够为所有参与者提供实践性学习体验。
它使学习者能够在没有任何风险的情况下探索、实验和练习。

q5.stem: What should participants do in a simulation to reap the greatest benefits possible?
options: Take the experience as a mere game.
Apply promptly what they learn to their jobs.
Develop a deep level of understanding.
Strive to connect closely with their leaders.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「To maximize benefits from simulation, participants should immediately apply the learning from the experience to forge a smooth link between learning and doing.」
排除：A：只是文中现象，不是为获得最大收益应采取的行动；C：是模拟可带来的体验，而非应当立即执行的动作；D：是成功模拟的条件，并非参与者为获益要做的行动
q5.stemCn: 参与者在模拟中应该做什么以获取最大的收益？
optionsCn: 仅仅将这种体验视为一场游戏。
迅速将他们所学到的应用到工作中。
培养深层次的理解。
努力与他们的领导保持紧密联系。

items.cn:
模拟器最常用于核能、航空和外科手术等行业，在这些行业中，失败会导致灾难性的后果。为了从模拟学习体验中获取最大价值，参与者应当立即并直接将其所学知识应用于组织内的具体干预措施中。
大多数组织都渴望推行重大的变革计划，却发现这些计划几乎无法实施。这在很大程度上是因为成功的变革不仅需要愿景，还需要一支不仅不抵制变革、反而拥抱变革的员工队伍。
要取得成功，组织必须建立一项转型计划，使变革能够迅速在其各部门和各层级间推进。无论高层管理的承诺程度如何，除非各层级的关键思想领袖都拥抱变革，否则这一倡议将会枯萎并消亡。为了激发这种广泛的激情，学习领导者必须让员工接触到“可能是什么”，这将使他们重新思考自己的心智模式，摆脱根深蒂固的范式，并抓住学习的机会。
让参与者进入一个模拟环境，为他们提供了体验另一种现实的机会，这可以促使他们重新思考当前的信念。
对大多数成年人来说，行为改变并不容易。讲座、培训项目和研讨会可以解释转型的智力要素，但它们很少能有效触及重大变革计划核心的行为层面。此外，在正常的工作条件下，管理者很少能看到员工发展努力的全面效果。因此，像模拟这样的干预措施可以为变革提供刺激。
作为一种学习工具，有效的模拟甚至优于经验，因为它加速了时间，压缩了空间，并且不同于现实，它是专门设计来最大化参与者学习的。模拟提供了一种沉浸式的学习体验，其中技能、流程和知识都能以现实无法做到的方式被凸显出来。在无限且无风险的模型中探索、实验并反复应用新知识的能力，使得模拟成为最高效的学习形式之一。
精心设计的模拟可以使个人和团队深入理解他们的决策以及对商业刺激的直觉反应如何影响其他参与者和整个组织。然而，要从中获益，模拟必须感觉像真实情况一样。在一次成功的模拟结束时，参与者必须声明“这就是我们”。如果他们不这么说，他们就会把这次经历视为一场游戏，这很难在工作中应用，或者更糟糕的是，被认为与日常工作任务无关。为了从模拟中获得最大益处，参与者应立即将此次体验中的所学应用到工作中，从而在学习和实践之间建立顺畅的联系。

items.src: 2025年6月 六级真题第3套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2025年6月 六级真题第3套 · 第2篇
items.text:
GDP growth is not a good indicator of how well a country is performing, and should not be the primary goal of governments. Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models. But while a sustainable economy is vital to our future, it is a means to an end, not an end in itself.
The idea that governments should focus on happiness has its critics. There are concerns about how happiness can be measured. Is happiness not a fleeting and subjective psychological state? Don't different people experience different levels of happiness? Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.
Of course, governments cannot impose life satisfaction on citizens. But our happiness relies on collaborative efforts as a society. A government's obligation lies in creating conditions that promote prosperity. And there is good reason to suppose that such conditions exist, are globally applicable, and are discoverable through research.
In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on 'real wealth' for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth. Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well. Technological advances and changes in social behavior enable us to make more efficient use of the assets that we already have. And focusing on access to the resources people need to live better lives could help reduce inequality.
As far as it goes, this has much in common with proposals tabled by 'happiness' advocates. But it sets the bar far too low for what governments can and should be doing for their citizens.
For example, it's not clear how a 'real wealth' economy would remedy the epidemic of mental ill-health that plagues our society. In Western countries, at least—poor mental health is more detrimental to wellbeing than poverty. Over and above a vastly improved provision of therapeutic mental healthcare, there are preventative measures for improving mental health that governments could and should adopt. The WHO recommends establishing institutions that facilitate community participation—educational programs and interventions that provide skills for promoting mental wellbeing. It says a lot, however, that the WHO feels the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to persuade governments that the cost of taking proposed measures is justified. As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity.
To demand that governments set the 'happiness' of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.

q5.stem: What does the passage say is the more recent thinking of economic growth?
options: It should be made sustainable.
It is vital to the future of humanity.
It should be governments' chief concern.
It is an indicator of government performance.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Unlimited growth is not sustainable, and economic thinking is moving toward the idea that we should aim for sustainability in our economic models.」
排除：A：B项“对将来关键”指可持续经济，非增长思路；B：C项“政府首要目标”被原文否定；C：D项“GDP指标好”与原文相反。
q5.stemCn: 文章指出，关于经济增长的更近期的想法是什么？
optionsCn: 它应该是可持续的。
它对人类的未来至关重要。
它应该是政府的首要关切。
它是衡量政府绩效的一个指标。

q5.stem: Why are some people opposed to the idea that governments should focus on happiness?
options: Governments cannot impose happiness on citizens.
People's happiness is built upon their own endeavor.
Happiness means different things to different people.
Happiness depends on sustainable economic growth.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Even on the broadest interpretation of 'happiness' as prosperity or 'life satisfaction', people want different things.」
排除：A：不能推出，政府不能强加幸福不是反对理由；B：无依据，原文强调幸福主观而非个人努力；D：无依据，原文反对增长至上，未说幸福依赖增长。
q5.stemCn: 为什么有些人反对政府应关注幸福的观点？
optionsCn: 政府不能把幸福强加给公民。
人们的幸福建立在他们自身的努力之上。
幸福对不同的人来说意味着不同的事情。
幸福取决于可持续的经济增长。

q5.stem: What does philosopher Julian Baggini suggest governments do in a recently published article?
options: Try to reduce inequality between the rich and the poor.
Provide people with access to resources for a better life.
Change people's behaviors to put social wealth to better use.
Make use of advanced technologies to improve people's lives.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「In a recently published article, philosopher Julian Baggini suggests we should focus on 'real wealth' for citizens, which does not depend on GDP growth. Access is key: people do not need to own, but rather access things that enable them to live well.」
排除：A：原文强调可及资源，不是让政府首要追求幸福；C：技术与社会行为变化只是条件，不是核心建议；D：降低不平等只是可能效果，非题干直接主张
q5.stemCn: 哲学家朱利安·巴吉尼在最近发表的一篇文章中建议政府做什么？
optionsCn: 试图缩小贫富差距。
为人们提供改善生活的资源途径。
改变人们的行为，以便更好地利用社会财富。
利用先进技术来改善人们的生活。

q5.stem: Why does the WHO feel the need to appeal to the economic benefits of improving mental health to justify its recommendations?
options: Mental health programs cannot be executed without GDP growth.
Psychological interventions are conducive to people's wellbeing.
Poor mental health is detrimental to a nation's economic system.
Governments still take economic development as their priority.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「As long as the economy is their priority, governments need go no further than ensuring citizens' continued productivity.」
排除：A：原文未说没有GDP增长就无法实施项目。；B：题干问WHO为何诉诸经济效益，非干预效果。；C：原文说损害福祉，非损害经济体系。
q5.stemCn: 为什么世界卫生组织觉得有必要诉诸于改善心理健康带来的经济利益，来证明其建议的合理性？
optionsCn: 没有GDP增长，心理健康项目就无法执行。
心理干预有利于人们的福祉。
糟糕的心理健康状况损害一个国家的经济体系。
政府仍然将经济发展作为优先事项。

q5.stem: What message does the author try to convey at the end of the passage?
options: Governments' goal should be prosperity-driven.
Governments' goal should be people-oriented.
Governments should consider citizens' views in decision-making.
Governments should set sustained productivity as their top priority.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「To demand that governments set the 'happiness' of citizens as their highest priority is to demand that they view citizens as ends in themselves.」
排除：A：作者反对以GDP/繁荣为首要目标；C：作者强调公民是目的，非仅收集主观意见；D：政府优先经济只是手段，不能最高优先级
q5.stemCn: 作者在文章结尾试图传达什么信息？
optionsCn: 政府的目标应该是由繁荣驱动的。
政府的目标应该是以人为本的。
政府在决策时应考虑公民的意见。
政府应将持续的生产力设定为首要任务。

items.cn:
GDP增长并不是衡量一个国家表现好坏的良好指标，也不应成为政府的首要目标。无限的增长是不可持续的，经济思维正朝着我们应该在经济模式中追求可持续性的理念转变。虽然可持续经济对我们的未来至关重要，但它只是达到目的的手段，而非目的本身。
主张政府应关注幸福的观点存在批评者。人们担心幸福该如何衡量。幸福难道不是一种短暂且主观的心理状态吗？不同的人难道不会体验到不同程度的幸福吗？即使是对“幸福”最宽泛的解释——如繁荣或“生活满意度”，人们想要的东西也是不同的。
当然，政府不能强加给公民生活满意度。但我们的幸福依赖于作为社会的协作努力。政府的义务在于创造促进繁荣的条件。而且有充分理由认为，这样的条件是存在的，具有全球适用性，并且可以通过研究被发现。
在一篇最近发表的文章中，哲学家朱利安·巴吉尼建议我们应关注公民的“真实财富”，这不依赖于GDP增长。获取（使用权）是关键：人们不需要拥有事物，而是需要获取那些使他们能良好生活的事物。技术进步和社会行为的变化使我们能够更高效地利用现有的资产。专注于获取人们过上更好生活所需的资源，有助于减少不平等。
就其范围而言，这与“幸福”倡导者提出的提议有很多共同之处。但它对政府能够且应该为公民做的事情设定了过低的门槛。
例如，目前尚不清楚“真实财富”经济如何补救困扰我们社会的心理健康疾病流行。至少在西方国家，较差的心理健康状况比贫困更损害幸福感。除了大幅改善治疗性心理健康服务外，政府还可以且应该采取一些预防性措施来改善心理健康。世界卫生组织建议建立促进社区参与的机构——即提供技能以促进心理健康的教育项目和干预措施。然而，值得注意的是，世界卫生组织感到有必要诉诸于改善心理健康带来的经济效益，以说服政府采取拟议措施的代价是合理的。只要经济仍是政府的首要任务，政府只需确保公民持续的生产力即可，无需更进一步。
要求政府将公民的“幸福”置于其首要位置，就是要求他们将公民视为目的本身。

items.src: 2025年12月 六级真题第1套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2025年12月 六级真题第1套 · 第1篇
items.text:
Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.
Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.
Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success". I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.
We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.

q5.stem: What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success?
options: They lack a shoulder to cry on.
They have no soul to confide in.
They cannot find reliable friends.
They ignore their ties with friends.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.」
排除：A：文首说友谊可作倾诉对象，非成功导致缺少肩膀；B：文章有可倾诉之人，未称完全没有灵魂可倾诉；C：文中是途中失去朋友，非找不到可靠朋友
q5.stemCn: 当人们渴望追求个人成功时，通常会发生什么？
optionsCn: 他们缺乏可以倾诉的朋友。
他们没有可以信赖的灵魂伴侣。
他们找不到可靠的朋友。
他们忽视了与朋友之间的联系。

q5.stem: What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism?
options: Reexamine its detrimental effects.
Shrug off the loss of their loved ones.
Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved.
Remove aggressive obstacles in the way.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.」
排除：B：作者批评学生借口语气，非建议漠视亲友；C：混乱是现实障碍，作者未建议规避；D：作者主张重估危害，未提移除外部障碍。
q5.stemCn: 作者建议人们在追求极端个人主义时做什么？
optionsCn: 重新审视其有害影响。
对失去亲人这件事耸肩表示无所谓。
避免其中涉及的混乱和动荡。
清除道路上的激进障碍。

q5.stem: What is American society's assumption of personal achievement?
options: It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended.
It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream.
It revolves around an individualistic culture.
It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.」
排除：A：原文称社会会庆祝个人成就，但此非成就背后的假设；B：原文未称个人成就是实现梦想的可靠途径；C：个体主义是文化背景，假设强调比他人更努力，C偷换概念。
q5.stemCn: 美国社会对个人成就的假设是什么？
optionsCn: 它理应得到庆祝和高度赞扬。
它是实现个人梦想的确定途径。
它围绕着一种个人主义文化。
它反映了一个人的非凡努力。

q5.stem: What is preached in many success stories?
options: Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success.
Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends.
Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success.
Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.」
排除：A：未说成功故事宣扬重视学业收获；C：未说应强化友情；D：未说以名校成绩为要。
q5.stemCn: 在许多成功故事中宣扬的是什么？
optionsCn: 在通往成功的道路上重视学术收获。
将时间投入工作而不是与朋友交往。
在追求个人成功的过程中努力加强友谊。
通过优异的学业成绩进入名牌大学。

q5.stem: What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success?
options: No one can succeed without pushing limits.
No one can afford to neglect close friends.
Collectivism is superior to individualism.
Success experts often lead people to ruin.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.」
排除：A：文章未证明不挑战极限就无人能成功；C：批评极端个人主义不等于断言集体主义更优；D：反对成功学观点不等于说专家常引人毁灭
q5.stemCn: 关于追求成功，我们可以从文章中推断出什么？
optionsCn: 没有人能在不挑战极限的情况下取得成功。
没有人可以忽视亲密的朋友。
集体主义优于个人主义。
成功专家常常把人引向毁灭。

items.cn:
许多人将友谊视为舒适的依靠：一个可以哭泣时倚靠的肩膀，一个可以倾诉衷肠的可靠灵魂。然而，更多时候，在我们急于追求个人成功的过程中，我们在路上失去了朋友，而这已成为这一过程的一部分。
伴随日常生活而来的混乱和无休止的动荡，是追求稳定友谊的一大阻碍。作为学生，我们常以此为借口，对那些我们曾视为挚爱的人的离去耸肩了事。
我们必须重新学会珍视在人生赛道上建立的联系，而不是把生活看作一场人人独自奔向某种成功的竞赛。我们必须重新评估极端个人自由带来的危害。
极端个人主义将个人的自由置于集体之上。例如，它主张普遍医疗保健——集体主义的一个例子——威胁了许多美国人的梦想。
我们中的许多人都成了个人主义文化的受害者。社会往往颂扬个人成就，并基于“获胜或成功源于比他人更努力”这一假设来推崇这种成就。
作为一个社会，我们将“在通往成功的道路上失去朋友”这一概念奉为圭臬。我记得在高一时听到过这样的话：“别担心失去友谊，只要专注于学习并考上大学。从长远来看，那才是唯一重要的事情。”这种观点并非我经历中独有的。它在许多成功故事中被宣扬，并已嵌入我们看待成长的方式之中。励志演讲者会促使听众对失去朋友这一必然结局安之若素。花太多时间与朋友相处？你是在浪费本可用于成就更好的时光。花时间经营人际关系？不如把时间花在事业上。
这种不断追求成功的需要使我们变得盲目，无法看清伴随日常生活的变革漩涡。人们期望我们切实地取得成功、赢得奖项、获得更高的职位和更好的成绩。为了成功，我们失去了朋友，而令人悲哀的是，这已被常态化。
我们不能对失去友谊安之若素，因为友谊是我们的锚点。是的，要追求成功，挑战自我，突破极限。但与那些自封的成功学专家相反，独自奋斗并不会让你比那些在他人的帮助下取得成功的人更成功或更优秀。
要在繁忙得似乎无暇顾及他人的日程表中，努力培养健康的人际关系并加以维持。尽管我们可能生活在一个珍视独立追求成就的社会中，但在旅途中有人支持和爱你，远比任何最终结果重要得多。

items.src: 2025年12月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2025年12月 六级真题第1套 · 第2篇
items.text:
During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality."
More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.
Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation. It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
Students — and adults for that matter — simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events. It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.
With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.
Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.
We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.
On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."

q5.stem: What does the author think about today's America?
options: It is struggling to transform fiction into reality.
It has been the focus of many vital conversations.
It still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized.
It has got to a point where people disagree on nearly every issue.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.」
排除：A：只停留在表象或局部，未指向公平未竟；B：与原文对后种族社会的否定相悖；D：偏离作者对美国公平现状的总体判断
q5.stemCn: 作者如何看待今天的美国？
optionsCn: 它正努力将虚构变为现实。
它是许多重要对话的焦点。
在真正实现公平之前，它还有很长的路要走。
它已经到了人们在几乎所有问题上都无法达成一致的地步。

q5.stem: What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years?
options: They have been unfairly treated regarding higher education.
They have been battling hard to address equity issues.
They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars.
They have come to see the consequences of racial discrimination.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.」
排除：B：文章未说黑人学生主动应对公平问题；C：原文为假设若解决本可增收，并非已增收；D：文章谈教育公平，未说学生已看清种族歧视。
q5.stemCn: 关于过去20年的黑人学生，我们从文章中学到了什么？
optionsCn: 他们在高等教育方面受到了不公平对待。
他们一直在努力解决公平问题。
他们将终身收入提高了数十亿美元。
他们开始认识到种族歧视的后果。

q5.stem: How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them?
options: By dealing with the thorny issues confronting them.
By seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony.
By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause.
By striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.」
排除：A：原文指错失弥合分歧的机会，非仅处理问题；B：原文未说抓住一切机会促进种族和谐；D：原文说错失机会，非追求识别价值机会。
q5.stemCn: 美国人如何弥合分歧？
optionsCn: 通过处理他们面临的棘手问题。
通过抓住每一个增进种族和谐的机会。
通过继续追求马丁·路德·金的事业。
通过努力识别极具价值的机会。

q5.stem: How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey?
options: It is compelled to address its historical social issues.
It is delaying advancements toward racial equality.
It has kept itself from polarization.
It has become increasingly split.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before".」
排除：A：调查未显示美国被迫处理历史社会问题。；B：延迟进步是作者判断，非调查对国家状态。；C：调查称美国更分裂，并非已避免极化。
q5.stemCn: 根据最近的一项调查，大多数美国人如何看待美国作为一个国家？
optionsCn: 它被迫解决其历史上的社会问题。
它正在拖延迈向种族平等的进步。
它避免了极化。
它变得越来越分裂。

q5.stem: What does the author suggest Americans do?
options: Ensure the well-being of their children and grandchildren.
Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues.
Restrain their intolerance and discrimination.
Restore social order for a harmonious nation.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo.」
排除：A：儿童议题只是细节；C：个人偏见只是原因之一；D：恢复秩序非作者主张
q5.stemCn: 作者建议美国人做什么？
optionsCn: 确保他们的子孙后代的福祉。
共同努力解决国家的公平问题。
克制他们的不容忍和歧视行为。
恢复社会秩序以建立和谐的国家。

items.cn:
马丁·路德·金小在诺贝尔和平奖获奖感言中说：“我相信，非暴力的真理和无条件的爱将在现实中占据主导地位。”
半个多世纪过去了，我们的社会仍在努力区分真理与幻想、事实与虚构。从气候变化争端到关于奴隶制教学方式的辩论，美国正处于十字路口。而公平之争正是这些至关重要对话的核心。
一项又一项研究表明，不平等造成了惊人的后果。花旗银行2020年的一份报告指出，如果过去二十年 adequately addressed（充分解决）了与高等教育相关的不平等问题，“黑人学生的终身收入本可增加900亿至1130亿美元”。
这一统计数据代表了我们作为一个国家未能正视的大量问题。它也突出了一个真相：我们正在错失弥合分歧、消除隔阂的宝贵机会。然而，通过尊崇金的遗产，我们可以让国家重回通向真正平等的道路。
学生——以及成年人——如果不了解当今冲突产生的根源，就无法理解这些冲突。这意味着我们有责任帮助他们建立美国历史与当前事件之间的联系。这也意味着为他们提供所需工具，以应对他们生活中的不平等和偏见。坚持这些原则，加上致力于真诚的对话，可以帮助每位学生更好地体会我们已取得的进步，并更清晰地看到尚未走过的道路。
通过对需要更多高素质、多元化教育工作者进行更真实的分析，我们可以改善全国学校的招聘、培训和留任策略。
不幸的是，根深蒂固的分歧正在延缓这些进展。最近的一项调查发现，77%的美国人认为国家“比以往任何时候都更加分裂”。但关于两极分化加剧的报道不应说服我们对彼此视而不见。相反，它们应促使我们直面共同的问题。
正如某些人所建议的那样，我们并没有生活在“后种族社会”。在种族不平等问题上，我们绝不能继续把头埋在沙子里。除非我们对不容忍、偏见以及这些社会弊病如何影响我们对待彼此的方式保持诚实，否则不公正将继续困扰我们。但我们的孩子和孙辈值得拥有更好的未来。
在这个马丁·路德·金纪念日及以后的日子里，让我们承诺共同努力打破现状。让我们继续建设一个更好、更具包容性的国家；用马丁·路德·金小的话说，建设“一个与自己和平相处的社会，一个能与其良知共存的社会”。

items.src: 2025年12月 六级真题第2套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2025年12月 六级真题第2套 · 第1篇
items.text:
As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others. We like to work with people who are like-minded, with whom we share a common interest, or who also believe in a cause we are serious about. This is evident in how we have organized ourselves into various collective groups such as nations, regions, communities, organizations, and families.
Does the group you belong to have a strong collective consciousness or shared beliefs? Is there interdependence among its members? Do you consider this group a significant part of your existence? If your answers are affirmative, then you are experiencing a micro version of solidarity.
What is solidarity? Its simplest definition in the dictionary is: "… a unifying opinion, feeling, purpose or interest among a group of people."
In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.
One facet of solidarity fits well with the principles of communitarianism(社群主义). In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good. However, its strict adherence to social cohesiveness and exclusiveness restricts expression and practice of individual differences and preferences. Consequently, individuality and autonomy are sacrificed to maintain the unity of the group.
Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice. It goes against the liberal idea of unrestricted individuals who see society as a hindrance to their freedom to make choices and to act according to what is good for them regardless of how these will affect others.
But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society. They believe that for human society to survive as it becomes more diverse, more new bonds need to be formed based on the differences. In the light of this, they regard a genuine solidarity as more than just shallow relationships based on common interests. Solidarity is not just a product of strategic calculations of how much it will benefit the self. It is not an exclusive class founded on the you-and-me-against-the-world principle. Rather, it is inclusive and is not forced. Acting out of solidarity means supporting and standing up for each other — in recognition that one's fate is in the fate of the other. It is a bond characterized by cooperative practices and strengthened by the concern for the well-being of others or the common good. It fights for the protection of human dignity and listens to and acts on the cries of the most vulnerable.

q5.stem: What does the author say about human beings?
options: They cannot prosper without cooperating with each other.
They share a common interest and believe in a just cause.
They think and behave alike in different social groups.
They cannot gain independence without fighting for it.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「As interdependent beings we cannot thrive independent of others.」
排除：B：原文只说喜欢与志同道合者共事，非人人共享同一兴趣或正义事业。C：文中有不同集体，非思想行为完全相同。D：强调相互依存，未说独立需要斗争。
q5.stemCn: 关于人类，作者说了什么？
optionsCn: 如果不彼此合作，人类就无法繁荣。
他们拥有共同的利益并相信正义的事业。
他们在不同的社会群体中思想和行为方式相似。
如果不为之奋斗，人类就无法获得独立。

q5.stem: What do we learn about solidarity in an increasingly diverse society?
options: It gives rise to a complicated division of labor.
It involves many aspects with great complexity.
It brings individuals together as environment changes.
It embraces the characteristics of different individuals.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「In this increasingly diverse society we live in, solidarity takes on a complex and multifaceted character as it forms bonds of interdependence among unique individuals living in a fast-changing environment and working within a complex division of labor.」
排除：A：偏离多样社会句，原文属另一层面；C：非该句直接支持的团结特征；D：原文另有表述，非题干所指
q5.stemCn: 关于日益多元化的社会中的团结，我们了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它导致了复杂的劳动分工。
它涉及许多方面且具有极大的复杂性。
随着环境的变化，它将个体凝聚在一起。
它包容了不同个体的特征。

q5.stem: What would we witness in the setting of communitarianism?
options: Ruling of social norms and ridding of individuality.
Emphasis on the adherence to individual differences.
Sacrifice of personal interests for the common good.
Elimination of individualism and personal choices.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「In this setting, individuals give up their own interests to serve the common good.」
排除：A：社会规范统治并非直接表述，原文只提牺牲个性。；B：原文强调限制个体差异，并非强调遵循差异。；D：原文说牺牲个性自主，不是消除个人主义与选择。
q5.stemCn: 在社群主义的背景下，我们会目睹什么？
optionsCn: 社会规范的统治和个性的消除。
强调坚持个体差异。
为共同利益牺牲个人利益。
消除个人主义和个人选择。

q5.stem: What does solidarity entail according to the passage?
options: A limit to personal differences.
An opposition to individualism.
A hindrance to social advancement.
An inevitable end to liberal pursuits.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「Solidarity is also viewed as a reaction to the extreme emphasis on individualism and freedom of choice.」
排除：A：原文只指社群主义式团结限制差异，并非团结的必然特征。；C：原文说团结促进秩序与进步，并非社会发展的阻碍。；D：原文仅反对极端个人主义，未说必然终结自由追求。
q5.stemCn: 根据文章，团结意味着什么？
optionsCn: 对个人差异的限制。
对个人主义的反对。
对社会进步的阻碍。
自由追求的必然终结。

q5.stem: What do social theorists think of solidarity?
options: It is especially relevant to the most vulnerable.
It is most effective in protecting human dignity.
It is essential to progress and order in society.
It is indispensable to avoiding shallow relationships.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「But despite its many facets, social theorists have viewed solidarity as a key factor in bringing about order and progress in society.」
排除：A：只是关注弱者，非社会学家观点；B：保护尊严无最有效比较；D：避免浅关系并非其核心观点。
q5.stemCn: 社会理论家如何看待团结？
optionsCn: 它与最脆弱的群体尤其相关。
它在保护人类尊严方面最有效。
它对社会的进步和秩序至关重要。
它是避免肤浅人际关系所不可或缺的。

items.cn:
作为相互依存的个体，我们无法脱离他人而繁荣发展。我们喜欢与志趣相投的人共事，这些人要么与我们有共同的兴趣，要么也认同我们严肃对待的事业。这一点在我们如何将自己组织成国家、地区、社区、组织和家庭等各种集体群体中体现得淋漓尽致。
你所归属的群体是否拥有强烈的集体意识或共同信念？其成员之间是否存在相互依赖关系？你是否认为这个群体是你存在的重要组成部分？如果你的回答是肯定的，那么你正在体验一种微缩版的团结。
什么是团结？词典中最简单的定义是：“……一群人之间统一的观点、情感、目的或利益。”
在我们所处的日益多样化的社会中，随着团结在快速变化的环境中独特的个体之间形成相互依存的纽带，并在复杂的劳动分工中发挥作用，它呈现出复杂且多面的特征。
团结的一个方面非常契合社群主义的原则。在这种情境下，个人放弃自身利益以服务于公共利益。然而，其对社交凝聚力排他性的严格坚持，限制了个人差异和偏好的表达与实践。因此，为了维持群体的统一，个性和自主性被牺牲了。
团结也被视为对极端强调个人主义和选择自由的回应。它反对自由主义的观念，即认为不受限制的个体将社会视为阻碍他们做出选择并按照对自己有益的方式行事（无论这些行为如何影响他人）的因素。
但尽管有多重面貌，社会理论家仍将团结视为带来社会秩序进步的关键因素。他们认为，为了使人类社会在变得更加多样化时得以生存，需要基于差异建立更多新的纽带。鉴于此，他们将真正的团结视为超越仅仅基于共同利益的浅层关系的东西。团结不仅仅是关于能为自己带来多少利益的战略计算产物。它也不是建立在“你和我对抗全世界”原则上的排他性阶层。相反，它是包容性的，且非强制性的。出于团结行动意味着互相支持和挺身而出——承认一个人的命运存在于另一个人的命运之中。这是一种以合作实践为特征、并通过关心他人福祉或公共利益而加强的纽带。它为保护人类尊严而战，倾听并采取行动回应最弱势群体的呼声。

items.src: 2025年12月 六级真题第2套 · 第2篇
items.title: 2025年12月 六级真题第2套 · 第2篇
items.text:
People who repeatedly give unwanted advice can be well-meaning and genuinely want to help. Others might do this out of a sense of self-worth around the ability to influence others. One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.
Under the guise(外表) of unselfishness, people may be driven to give you unwanted advice because it makes them feel powerful or in control. They may not be fully aware of this drive, however.
These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down. It is possible that their emotions were only validated in childhood when they were at their loudest, encouraging them to adopt responses to discomfort that are excessive in most situations.
When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.
If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.
The key is to validate without over-identifying. You can let them know that you have heard them and appreciate where they are coming from without taking on the potentially damaging narrative that you could not have gotten by without their help. You had better say something like, "Thanks for the idea. I have my own plan for handling this, but I really appreciate your perspective and will take it into consideration. Can I let you know when I need help in the future?"
If you have trouble setting boundaries tactfully, prioritize working on your own ability to self-regulate. As uncomfortable as it may be to continuously receive, if you can respond with compassion, the situation will likely defuse much faster.
Though it is usually not the intended outcome of giving unsolicited advice, many who receive it often feel stressed, offended, or simply annoyed by unwanted suggestions. Setting a boundary in this regard, if you feel you need one, is perfectly reasonable and something that can bring you increased emotional safety.
It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.

q5.stem: What is the finding of one study about people who keep giving unsolicited advice?
options: They turn out to be well-meaning.
They are genuinely kind-hearted.
They are capable of influencing others.
They are inclined to crave for power.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「One study found that people with a high tendency to seek power were more likely to give advice than those with an opposite tendency.」
排除：A：原文只称可能出于好意，未说必然好意；B：原文只称可能真诚善良，未说必然如此；C：研究未说其有能力影响他人，只提寻求权力。
q5.stemCn: 一项关于总是提供未经请求的建议的人的研究发现了什么？
optionsCn: 事实证明他们是出于好意。
他们确实是心地善良的。
他们有能力影响他人。
他们倾向于渴望权力。

q5.stem: What is the problem with people who are driven to give you unsolicited advice?
options: They may be quick to upset others.
They may be emotionally vulnerable.
They want their voice to be the loudest.
They respond to discomfort excessively.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「These people may also display a problematic degree of emotional vulnerability, becoming upset very quickly, and taking a long time to calm down.」
排除：A：原文指易自己情绪受挫，非快速惹怒他人。；C：童年被认可不等于现在追求声音最大。；D：原文是情绪易受挫且难平静，非泛称过度应对不适。
q5.stemCn: 那些被迫给你提供未经请求的建议的人存在什么问题？
optionsCn: 他们可能很容易惹恼别人。
他们在情感上可能很脆弱。
他们希望自己的声音最大。
他们对不适反应过度。

q5.stem: What is the advice receiver tempted to do when noticing the advice giver's underlying anxiety?
options: Reveal the undesired result of their approach.
Refuse their advice in an undisguised manner.
Bring their real motives to the surface.
Accuse them of trying to control others.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「When someone is giving advice in order to make themselves feel more powerful, there is underlying anxiety to their behavior that recipients of the advice tend to notice. It can be tempting in this situation to react harshly to the advice giver and to accuse them of being manipulative, but this approach might produce an undesired result.」
排除：A：揭露不良后果并非被诱惑反应，只是可能结果；B：直率拒绝属后续风险，非察觉焦虑后诱惑；C：原文只说易察觉焦虑，未说会揭穿动机
q5.stemCn: 当建议接收者注意到建议提供者潜在的焦虑时，他们倾向于做什么？
optionsCn: 揭示其方法的不理想结果。
以毫不掩饰的方式拒绝他们的建议。
将他们的真实动机暴露出来。
指责他们试图控制他人。

q5.stem: How is the advice giver likely to react to the rejection of their advice?
options: They may regard it as a threat.
They may modify their behavior.
They get ready for a larger conflict.
They begin to doubt their self-worth.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「If the act of giving advice is contributing actively to someone's feelings of self-worth, an outright(直率的) rejection may be perceived as a threat, activating their fight-or-flight response, possibly causing them to double down on their validation-seeking behavior, or leading to a larger conflict.」
排除：A：未提建议者会修改行为，可能加倍寻求认可。；B：原文是可能导致冲突，并非准备好更大冲突。；C：未提拒绝使其怀疑自我价值，只称拒绝被视作威胁。
q5.stemCn: 建议提供者对被拒绝的反应可能是怎样的？
optionsCn: 他们可能将其视为一种威胁。
他们可能会改变自己的行为。
他们准备好进行更大规模的冲突。
他们开始怀疑自我价值。

q5.stem: What should the advice receiver do to avoid unnecessary conflict?
options: Concede the advice is perfectly reasonable.
Give their reasons for not taking the advice.
Understand why the advice giver offers the advice.
Explain their chosen way of handling the situation.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「It is best to set boundaries in a way that takes into account the individual's underlying reasons for doing what they are doing to avoid unnecessary conflict and more stress.」
排除：A：原文未要求承认建议合理，只需理解动机；B：拒收理由可能引发防御，增加冲突；D：说明处理方式是边界表达，不是避免冲突关键。
q5.stemCn: 为了避免不必要的冲突，建议接收者应该怎么做？
optionsCn: 承认该建议完全合理。
给出不接受该建议的理由。
理解建议提供者为何提出该建议。
解释他们处理这种情况的选择方式。

items.cn:
那些反复给出令人不快的建议的人可能是出于好意，真心想要提供帮助。另一些人这样做可能是出于一种通过影响他人来获得自我价值感的心态。一项研究发现，具有强烈追求权力倾向的人比具有相反倾向的人更可能给出建议。
在无私的外表之下，人们可能会被驱使去给你提供不请自来的建议，因为这让他们感到有权力或处于控制地位。然而，他们可能并未完全意识到这种驱动力。
