这类人也可能表现出一定程度的情绪脆弱性，容易迅速变得不安，并且需要很长时间才能平静下来。有可能在他们童年时期，只有当他们声音最大（情绪最激烈）时，他们的情绪才得到认可，这促使他们在大多数情况下采用过度的应对方式来处理不适感。
当某人为了让自己感觉更强大而给出建议时，其行为背后潜藏着焦虑，接受建议的人往往会察觉到这一点。在这种情况下，严厉地回应建议提供者并指责他们搞操纵是很诱人的，但这种做法可能会产生不良后果。
如果给予建议的行为正在积极促进某人的自我价值感，那么直接的拒绝可能会被视为一种威胁，激发他们的“战斗或逃跑”反应，可能导致他们加倍寻求确认的行为，或者引发更大的冲突。
关键在于在不进行过度认同的情况下给予肯定。你可以让他们知道你已经听到了他们的意见，并欣赏他们的出发点，但不要接受那种“如果没有他们的帮助你就无法度过难关”的潜在有害叙事。你最好这样说：“谢谢你的建议。我自己有处理这件事的计划，但我真的很感激你的观点，并会予以考虑。以后当我需要帮助时，我可以告诉你吗？”
如果你在委婉地设定界限方面有困难，请优先提升你自己自我调节的能力。尽管持续接收建议可能令人不适，但如果你能以同情心回应，局势很可能会更快地缓和。
虽然提供不请自来的建议通常并非有意为之，但许多接受者常常会因为这些不需要的建议而感到压力、被冒犯或仅仅是恼火。如果你觉得需要，在这方面设定界限是完全合理的，并且可以为你带来更多的情感安全感。
最好以一种考虑到对方行为背后根本原因的方式来设定界限，以避免不必要的冲突和更多的压力。

items.src: 2025年12月 六级真题第3套 · 第1篇
items.title: 2025年12月 六级真题第3套 · 第1篇
items.text:
Mindfulness has been shown to have a number of meaningful health benefits — it can help reduce anxiety and promote healing in those suffering from chronic illness.
The practice is based on an insight first described in ancient Buddhist texts that human beings have the capacity to observe experience without being caught up in it. This means simply that it is possible to observe ourselves having a craving, or a happy thought, or even a scary emotion, without reacting in the moment in a way that amplifies the feeling or sends the mind spiraling off into thinking about old memories or anticipating events.
This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.
One of the challenges of practicing mindfulness in our contemporary world is that there has been a profound transformation in human attention. The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell. This economy rests on a technological revolution of mobile phones and social media that makes it possible for corporations to target our attention with their content at every moment.
The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment. The result is that it can feel as though our ability to focus, and be fully present, has been stolen. But mindfulness can help us resist the attention economy and relish the things that make life special, like being together with those we love.
Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.
The sad truth is that living in the attention economy, most of us have become bad listeners. However, just as it is possible to watch ourselves having an experience without reacting, it's possible to watch another person have an experience without getting tied up in reactivity and judgment.
The gift of mindfulness is a practice of listening with compassion to others describe their experiences. To give this gift means putting away your phone, turning off social media, and setting aside other common distractions. It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.
If we judge the value of gifts based on their price, this gift may seem worthless, but in a distracted world, it is a precious one.

q5.stem: What do we learn from the passage about practicing mindfulness?
options: It triggers our mind to reflect on past experiences or anticipate future events.
It focuses our attention on the present moment without making judgments.
It concentrates our mind on our personal feelings, happy or scary.
It helps our mind to stay calm when facing judgments from others.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「This practice of mindfulness can help calm the mind and the body as we learn not to react to experience with likes and dislikes or judgments of good and bad. It does not make us cold or indifferent but more fully present.」
排除：A：正念是观察当下体验，非引发回忆或预期未来；C：正念是不被情绪左右，非专注个人感受；D：正念是放下自身判断，非应对他人评判。
q5.stemCn: 关于正念练习，我们从文章中了解到什么？
optionsCn: 它促使我们的头脑反思过去的经历或预判未来的事件。
它将我们的注意力集中在当下，而不做任何评判。
它让我们的头脑专注于个人的感受，无论是快乐还是恐惧。
它帮助我们的头脑在面对他人的评判时保持冷静。

q5.stem: What do we see in today's "attention economy" according to Jenny Odell?
options: Focus on technological advances continuously updates products and services.
People's attention is turned into something that can be bought and sold.
Businesses profit from selling mobile phones and revolutionizing social media.
People tend to purchase products and services without careful thinking.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「The artist Jenny Odell argues that in our "attention economy" human attention has been transformed into a commodity that big corporations buy and sell.」
排除：A：原文未提技术不断更新产品服务。；C：手机社媒只是使企业能瞄准注意力，非买卖对象。；D：未说人们未深思就购买产品服务。
q5.stemCn: 根据珍妮·奥德尔（Jenny Odell）的观点，在今天的“注意力经济”中我们看到了什么？
optionsCn: 对技术进步的持续关注不断更新产品和服务。
人们的注意力被转化为可以买卖的东西。
企业通过销售手机和革新社交媒体获利。
人们往往不经仔细思考就购买产品和服务。

q5.stem: What happens with the prevalent use of mobile phones or social media?
options: They keep distracting users from the here and now.
They render users incapable of resisting temptation.
They rob users of their ability to observe experience.
They tempt users to endorse the attention economy.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「The devices most people use are a perpetual diversion from the present moment.」
排除：B：原文未称手机让人无法抵抗诱惑。；C：文中说专注力被剥夺，未说失去观察体验能力。；D：未提及人们会因此支持注意力经济。
q5.stemCn: 随着手机或社交媒体的普遍使用，发生了什么？
optionsCn: 它们不断将用户从此时此地分心开来。
它们使用户无力抵抗诱惑。
它们剥夺了用户观察体验的能力。
它们诱使用户支持注意力经济。

q5.stem: What benefit can practicing mindfulness bring to us according to some scholars?
options: It prevents us from making arbitrary judgments about others.
It shifts our attention from material things to spiritual pursuits.
It is conducive to our forging better interpersonal relationships.
It is helpful in regaining our ability to enjoy what we have in life.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「Most mindfulness research focuses on the individual benefits of the practice, but some scholars assert that we can not only practice mindfulness for ourselves but also practice it for others. It can help us build stronger, healthier relationships.」
排除：A：原文说正念减少评判，未说防止武断评判他人；B：原文未说从物质转向精神；D：享受当下属抵抗注意力经济，未体现学者所说人际益处。
q5.stemCn: 根据一些学者的观点，练习正念能给我们带来什么好处？
optionsCn: 它能防止我们对他人做出武断的评判。
它能将我们的注意力从物质事物转移到精神追求上。
它有助于我们建立更好的人际关系。
它有助于我们重新获得享受生活中所拥有之物的能力。

q5.stem: What does the author suggest we do in another person's presence?
options: Share each other's experience frankly and compassionately.
Pay full attention to establishing close relationships with them.
Be attentive listeners while refraining from making judgments.
Remind them of the distraction from mobile phones and social media.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「It means practicing being fully present in another person's presence and listening to them with complete attention without judgment, while resisting the urge to make the interaction about you.」
排除：A：原文未把该项作为对“在场”的具体建议；B：该项是其他段落的信息，并非题干所指；D：该项虽被提及，但不是完整专注无评判地听。
q5.stemCn: 作者建议我们在他人面前怎么做？
optionsCn: 坦诚且富有同情心地分享彼此的经历。
全神贯注地与他们建立亲密关系。
做专注的倾听者，同时避免做出评判。
提醒他们注意来自手机和社交媒体的干扰。

items.cn:
正念已被证明具有许多有意义的健康益处——它可以帮助减轻焦虑，并促进慢性病患者的康复。
这一练习基于古老佛教经典中首先描述的一种洞见，即人类有能力观察体验而不被其裹挟。这意味着，我们可以简单地观察自己产生的渴望、快乐的念头，甚至是恐惧的情绪，而无需即时做出反应，从而放大这种感觉，或让思绪陷入对旧记忆的回想或对未来的预期之中。
这种正念练习可以通过学习不对体验以喜好厌恶或好坏评判的方式作出反应，来帮助平静身心。它不会让我们变得冷漠或无动于衷，而是让我们更加全然地在场。
在当今世界实践正念的一个挑战在于，人类的注意力发生了深刻的转变。艺术家珍妮·奥德尔（Jenny Odell）认为，在我们的“注意力经济”中，人类的注意力已转化为大公司买卖的商品。这种经济建立在手机和社交媒体引发的技术革命之上，使得公司能够随时随地用其内容锁定我们的注意力。
大多数人使用的设备是对当下的永恒干扰。结果是，我们似乎感到自己的专注力和全然在场的能力已被窃取。但正念可以帮助我们抵御注意力经济，享受那些让生活特别的事物，比如与我们所爱的人在一起。
大多数正念研究侧重于该练习对个人的益处，但一些学者断言，我们不仅可以为自己修习正念，也可以为他人修习正念。它有助于我们建立更牢固、更健康的人际关系。
令人悲伤的事实是，生活在注意力经济中，我们中的大多数人已成为糟糕的倾听者。然而，正如我们可以观察自己的体验而不作出反应一样，我们也可以观察他人的体验，而不陷入情绪反应和评判之中。
正念的礼物是一种带着慈悲心倾听他人描述其体验的实践。给予这份礼物意味着收起你的手机，关闭社交媒体，并摒弃其他常见的干扰因素。这意味着练习在他人面前保持全然的在场，并以完全不带评判的注意力去倾听他们，同时克制住将互动中心转向你自己的冲动。
如果我们根据价格来衡量礼物的价值，这份礼物可能看似一文不值，但在一个充满干扰的世界里，它却是珍贵的。

items.title: 2025年12月 六级真题第3套 · 第2篇
items.text:
The other day I had to log into a service I hadn't used before. Since I was a new user, the website decided that it needed to check I wasn't a robot and so set me a Captcha test to determine whether the user is a person or a machine.
I was presented with an image of a roadside scene over which was laid a grid. My "challenge" was to click on each cell in the grid that contained a traffic sign. I did so, a bit irritated. Then I was presented with another image and another grid — also with a request to identify road signs. Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.
And then I realised what I had been doing was adding to a dataset for training the machine-learning software that guides self-driving cars. So, to gain access to an automated service that will benefit financially from my input, I first have to do some unpaid labor to help improve the performance of autonomous vehicles.
Neat, eh? But note also the delicious additional irony that the Captcha is described as an "automated Turing test". The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!
The strangest aspect of this unparalleled shift is how under-discussed it has been. The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us? Have we been conditioned to accept a world governed by "smart" tech, trading convenience to the point where we become a bit like machines ourselves?
In a recent startling and thoughtful book, two scholars — Brett Frischmann, a law professor, and Evan Selinger, a philosopher — argue that the answer to that question is "yes".
And they're right. There's nothing technophobic(技术恐惧的) about that. We shape our tools and then our tools shape us. Technology is supposed to provide tools that serve human ends. But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours. In the process, they reduce us to the status of cheery rats running on treadmills(踏车) designed by people who do not have our interests at heart. So back to the frog metaphor. Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late? You don't even have to Google it to know the answer.

q5.stem: How did the author respond to the Captcha test?
options: He clicked on the cells randomly.
He accepted the challenge readily.
He completed it confidently.
He worked on it submissively.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「Like a lamb, I complied, after which the website accepted my input.」
排除：A：原文说他点击含路牌的单元格，并非随意乱点；B：他有些恼火，并非欣然接受挑战；C：原文未体现自信，只说像羔羊般顺从完成。
q5.stemCn: 作者是如何回应验证码测试的？
optionsCn: 他随机点击方格。
他欣然接受了挑战。
他自信地完成了测试。
他顺从地配合完成测试。

q5.stem: What is ironic about the Captcha test?
options: A machine can respond to the test as well as humans do.
A machine can outperform humans in object identification.
A test designed to test machines is now used by machines to test humans.
A test conceived to tell a human from a robot can now do tricks humans can't.
q5.explain:
正确答案 C。依据（原文）：「The Turing test was conceived, you may recall, as a way of enabling humans to determine whether a machine could respond in such a way that one couldn't tell whether it was a human or a robot. So we have wandered into a world in which machines make us do tricks to prove that we are humans!」
排除：A：原文未说机器能像人一样通过。；B：未比较机器与人在物体识别上的优劣。；D：不是人类无法做的诡计，而是证明是人。
q5.stemCn: 关于验证码测试，有什么讽刺之处？
optionsCn: 机器可以像人类一样很好地响应测试。
机器在物体识别方面可以超越人类。
原本设计用来测试机器的程序，现在却被机器用来测试人类。
原本旨在区分人类与机器人的测试，现在却能让机器人做出人类无法做到的诡计。

q5.stem: Why does the author use the metaphor of the boiling frog?
options: To show that humans are unwilling to trade convenience for control by smart tech.
To show that humans are unaware of the potential danger brought by smart tech.
To question whether humans are conditioned to accept digital tech.
To question whether humans are as vulnerable as the boiling frog.
q5.explain:
正确答案 B。依据（原文）：「The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?」
排除：A：未表达不愿，原文强调已用便利交换而不察觉；C：原文已认定被引导接受智能科技，非单纯质疑；D：喻意在逐渐不觉危险，非质疑人类脆弱
q5.stemCn: 作者为什么使用“温水煮青蛙”的比喻？
optionsCn: 为了表明人类不愿用控制权换取智能科技带来的便利。
为了表明人类没有意识到智能科技带来的潜在危险。
为了质疑人类是否已经习惯于接受数字技术。
为了质疑人类是否像温水中的青蛙一样脆弱。

q5.stem: Why does the author think that Brett Frischmann and Evan Selinger are right?
options: A large part of digital tech is now making use of humans to meet its own ends.
Humans are now fast locked in a race against digital tech to control the world.
Digital tech can serve human needs in ways previously thought impossible.
Digital tech is now doing thinking while humans are doing repetitive work.
q5.explain:
正确答案 A。依据（原文）：「But, as the machine-learning Captcha demonstrates, a significant proportion of digital tech now sees (and uses) humans as means to ends that are not ours.」
排除：B：原文未提人类与技术快速竞赛争夺世界控制权。；C：文中说技术应服务人类目的，未提其以前所未有方式满足需求。；D：原文只称人类被利用，未说数字技术正在思考。
q5.stemCn: 为什么作者认为布伦特·弗里希曼（Brett Frischmann）和埃文·塞林格（Evan Selinger）是正确的？
optionsCn: 目前大部分数字技术正在利用人类来实现其自身目的。
人类现在正迅速卷入一场与控制世界相关的数字技术竞赛。
数字技术以前所未有的方式服务于人类需求。
数字技术现在在进行思考，而人类则在做重复性工作。

q5.stem: What does the author imply by asking "Are we smart enough to jump out before it's too late?" at the end of the passage?
options: It is not sensible to expect digital tech to take humans' interest to heart.
It is hard to say whether technology or humans will get the upper hand.
We may have to search the web to get the answer to the question.
We may not awake in time to the danger digital tech poses to us.
q5.explain:
正确答案 D。依据（原文）：「The metaphor of the boiling frog comes to mind. Have we become so subtly conditioned by digital technology that we don't see what's been happening to us?」
排除：A：问句并非断言人已变成机器；B：也未说技术已完全支配人类；C：末句说不必搜索，C曲解原文
q5.stemCn: 作者在文章结尾提出“我们是否足够聪明，能在为时已晚之前跳出陷阱？”这一问题，暗示了什么？
optionsCn: 指望数字技术关心人类利益是不明智的。
很难说究竟是技术还是人类会占据上风。
我们可能需要上网搜索才能找到这个问题的答案。
我们可能无法及时醒悟到数字技术对我们构成的危险。

items.cn:
前几天，我不得不登录一个之前从未使用过的服务。由于我是新用户，网站决定需要验证我不是机器人，因此让我做了一个验证码测试，以确定用户是人还是机器。
屏幕上出现了一张路边场景的图片，上面覆盖着一个网格。我的“挑战”是点击网格中包含交通标志的每个单元格。我有些恼火地照做了。接着，我又看到另一张图片和另一个网格——同样要求识别路标。我像只温顺的小羊一样配合了操作，随后网站接受了我的输入。
然后我意识到，我所做的事情实际上是在为引导自动驾驶汽车的机器学习软件添加训练数据集。因此，为了获得一项能从我的输入中获得财务利益的自动化服务的访问权限，我首先得做一些无偿劳动，以帮助提高自动驾驶汽车的性能。
挺巧妙，是吧？但还请注意这层绝妙的额外讽刺意味：验证码被描述为一种“自动化的图灵测试”。你可能记得，图灵测试最初构想出来，是为了让人类判断一台机器能否以某种方式回应，以至于无法分辨它是人还是机器人。所以我们已经走进这样一个世界：机器让我们耍花招，以证明我们是人类！
这种前所未有的转变中最奇怪的一面，是其受到的讨论如此之少。我想到了“温水煮青蛙”的比喻。我们是否已经被数字技术如此微妙地条件反射化，以至于看不见正在发生在我们身上的事？我们是否已被驯化去接受一个由“智能”科技主导的世界，在这种交换便利的过程中，我们自己也变得有点像机器了？
在最近一本令人震惊且深思熟虑的书里，两位学者——法学教授布雷特·弗里希曼（Brett Frischmann）和哲学家埃文·塞林格（Evan Selinger）——辩称这个问题的答案是“是的”。
他们是对的。这并非出于技术恐惧症。我们塑造工具，然后工具塑造我们。技术本应提供服务于人类目的的工具。但是，正如用于机器学习的验证码所展示的那样，相当一部分数字技术现在将人类视为实现非我们自身目标的手段。在这个过程中，我们将自己降级为快乐的老鼠，在由并不关心我们利益的人设计的跑步机上奔跑。那么回到青蛙的比喻：我们是否足够聪明，能在为时已晚之前跳出锅外？你甚至不需要上网搜索就能知道答案。
